---- MODULE W4Od18m4p1t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Locks, MaxGen, MaxShed, MinLimit, MaxLimit

VARIABLES record, mark, version, queue, limit, shed

vars == <<record, mark, version, queue, limit, shed>>

\* A job is the app's read-modify-write intent: which lock, the generation it
\* computed, and the record version it read while computing.
Job == [lock: Locks, gen: 1..MaxGen, base: 0..MaxGen]

TypeOK ==
    /\ record \in [Locks -> 0..MaxGen]
    /\ mark \in [Locks -> 0..MaxGen]
    /\ version \in 0..MaxGen
    /\ queue \in Seq(Job)
    /\ limit \in MinLimit..MaxLimit
    /\ shed \in 0..MaxShed

Init ==
    /\ record = [l \in Locks |-> 0]
    /\ mark = [l \in Locks |-> 0]
    /\ version = 0
    /\ queue = <<>>
    /\ limit = MinLimit
    /\ shed = 0

Fresh(l) == [lock |-> l, gen |-> record[l] + 1, base |-> version]

Submit(l) ==
    /\ Len(queue) < limit
    /\ record[l] < MaxGen
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, Fresh(l))
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, mark, version, limit, shed>>

\* Backpressure: a job arriving at a full queue is refused, never buffered.
Shed ==
    /\ Len(queue) >= limit
    /\ shed < MaxShed
    /\ shed' = shed + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, mark, version, queue, limit>>

Commit ==
    /\ queue # <<>>
    /\ Head(queue).base = version
    /\ LET j == Head(queue) IN
        /\ record' = [record EXCEPT ![j.lock] = j.gen]
        /\ mark' = [mark EXCEPT ![j.lock] = IF j.gen > mark[j.lock]
                                            THEN j.gen ELSE mark[j.lock]]
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<limit, shed>>

\* The front job was computed against a record version that has since moved on.
Discard ==
    /\ queue # <<>>
    /\ Head(queue).base # version
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, mark, version, limit, shed>>

\* The admission limit is retuned live and may drop below the current backlog.
Retune ==
    /\ \E n \in MinLimit..MaxLimit : limit' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, mark, version, queue, shed>>

Next == \/ \E l \in Locks : Submit(l)
        \/ Shed \/ Commit \/ Discard \/ Retune

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No lost update: the live value never regresses below one already committed.
NoLostUpdate == \A l \in Locks : record[l] = mark[l]

StateBound == version <= MaxGen
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Locks = {frontDoor, backDoor}
    MaxGen = 3
    MaxShed = 2
    MinLimit = 1
    MaxLimit = 2

INVARIANT NoLostUpdate

CONSTRAINT StateBound
nl:
A smart-home door lock network keeps one shared configuration record that maps each lock to its current keypad-code generation number. A hub owns the record and stamps it with a version that advances by one every time a change is written. Because the radio link to the locks is slow, changes are not written directly: a phone app first reads the record, computes the new generation number for the lock it wants to change, and hands that change to the hub as a job. Each job therefore carries the lock it targets, the new generation number the app computed, and the record version the app read when it computed it.

The hub holds those jobs in a bounded work queue. The queue's admission limit is a live tuning parameter: a homeowner or an installer can raise it when the house is busy and lower it when the hub is thermally throttled, and the new limit takes effect immediately even if more jobs are already parked in the queue than the new limit allows. When a job arrives and the queue is already at its limit, the hub does not silently forget it and does not grow the queue; it applies backpressure, refusing the job outright and incrementing a shed counter that the app can read to learn it must retry.

The hub drains the queue from the front, one job at a time. Before writing a job it compares the version the job was computed against with the record's current version. If they match, the job is fresh: the hub writes the computed generation number into the record for that lock, advances the record version, and notes the value it just committed for that lock in a per-lock high-water mark. If they do not match, the record has moved on since the app read it, so the job is stale and the hub discards it from the front of the queue without writing anything; the app will observe the version change and recompute.

The full set of actions the hub network can take is: Submit, which places a fresh job on the queue while there is room under the current limit; Shed, which refuses an arriving job and bumps the shed counter when the queue is at its limit; Commit, which writes the front job when its base version matches the record version and advances both the record and the lock's high-water mark; Discard, which drops the front job when its base version is stale; and Retune, which changes the queue's admission limit at runtime to any value in the supported range.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every lock, the generation number currently stored in the shared record is exactly the highest generation number ever committed for that lock, so no committed change to a lock is ever clobbered by a job computed from an older view of the record.

---- MODULE W4Od6m7p4t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Cars, Riders, Occupancy

\* aboard: who is in each car; stamp: the car's compare-and-swap register;
\* channel: permits in flight, deliverable in any order.
VARIABLES aboard, stamp, channel, waiting, arrived

vars == <<aboard, stamp, channel, waiting, arrived>>

Permits == [rider: Riders, car: Cars, seen: 0..(2 * Cardinality(Riders))]

TypeOK ==
    /\ aboard \in [Cars -> SUBSET Riders]
    /\ stamp \in [Cars -> 0..(2 * Cardinality(Riders))]
    /\ channel \subseteq Permits
    /\ waiting \subseteq Riders
    /\ arrived \subseteq Riders

Init ==
    /\ aboard = [c \in Cars |-> {}]
    /\ stamp = [c \in Cars |-> 0]
    /\ channel = {}
    /\ waiting = Riders
    /\ arrived = {}

Outstanding(r) == \E p \in channel : p.rider = r

\* The dispatcher reads the stamp, sees room, and publishes a permit.
Issue(r, c) ==
    /\ r \in waiting
    /\ ~Outstanding(r)
    /\ Cardinality(aboard[c]) < Occupancy
    /\ channel' = channel \cup {[rider |-> r, car |-> c, seen |-> stamp[c]]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<aboard, stamp, waiting, arrived>>

\* The swap succeeds only if the stamp still matches what the permit saw.
Board(p) ==
    /\ p \in channel
    /\ p.rider \in waiting
    /\ stamp[p.car] = p.seen
    /\ aboard' = [aboard EXCEPT ![p.car] = @ \cup {p.rider}]
    /\ stamp' = [stamp EXCEPT ![p.car] = @ + 1]
    /\ waiting' = waiting \ {p.rider}
    /\ channel' = channel \ {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED arrived

Tear(p) ==
    /\ p \in channel
    /\ stamp[p.car] # p.seen
    /\ channel' = channel \ {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<aboard, stamp, waiting, arrived>>

Alight(c, r) ==
    /\ r \in aboard[c]
    /\ aboard' = [aboard EXCEPT ![c] = @ \ {r}]
    /\ stamp' = [stamp EXCEPT ![c] = @ + 1]
    /\ arrived' = arrived \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<channel, waiting>>

IssueStep == \E r \in Riders, c \in Cars : Issue(r, c)
BoardStep == \E p \in channel : Board(p)
TearStep  == \E p \in channel : Tear(p)

\* The rush is over: lobby empty and every car unloaded, so the bank idles.
Settled ==
    /\ waiting = {}
    /\ \A c \in Cars : aboard[c] = {}
    /\ channel = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next == IssueStep \/ BoardStep \/ TearStep \/ Settled
        \/ (\E c \in Cars, r \in Riders : Alight(c, r))

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ WF_vars(IssueStep) /\ WF_vars(BoardStep) /\ WF_vars(TearStep)

CapacityRespected == \A c \in Cars : Cardinality(aboard[c]) <= Occupancy

LobbyDrains == \A r \in Riders : (r \in waiting) ~> (r \notin waiting)
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Cars = {carA, carB}
    Riders = {r1, r2}
    Occupancy = 2

INVARIANT CapacityRespected

PROPERTY LobbyDrains
nl:
An elevator bank in a skyscraper serves a lobby crowd during the morning rush. Each car has a placarded occupancy limit that the building inspector treats as absolute. The dispatcher does not talk to the cars over a reliable ordered link; it publishes boarding permits onto a shared radio channel, and the cars pick permits off that channel in whatever order the radio happens to deliver them, so a permit issued first may well be honoured last.

To keep the occupancy limit honest despite that reordering, every car exposes a single compare-and-swap register holding a stamp that changes whenever the car's occupancy changes. When the dispatcher wants to send a rider to a car, it reads that car's stamp, checks that the car has room right now, and publishes a permit naming the rider, the car, and the stamp it read. A car honours a permit only if the stamp carried by the permit still equals the stamp in its register; that comparison is the swap's guard. If the stamps differ, the car's occupancy has moved since the permit was minted, the permit is torn up unused, and the dispatcher is free to mint a fresh one for that rider.

Riders leave cars too. When a rider reaches their floor they step out, which frees a slot and bumps the car's stamp, invalidating any permit that was minted against the old occupancy. The dispatcher never issues a second outstanding permit for a rider who already has one on the channel.

The full set of actions in this system is: Issue, in which the dispatcher reads a car's stamp, confirms the car is below its occupancy limit, and publishes a permit for a lobby rider who has no permit outstanding; Board, in which a car finds a permit whose stamp matches its register, admits the named rider, and bumps its stamp; Tear, in which a car discards a permit whose stamp no longer matches, freeing the named rider to be re-permitted; Alight, in which a rider aboard a car steps out at their floor, leaving the car and bumping its stamp; and Settled, in which the bank simply idles once the lobby is empty, every car is unloaded, and no permit is left on the channel.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every instant, the number of riders aboard any car is at most that car's placarded occupancy limit.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every rider waiting in the lobby eventually stops waiting, because permits keep being minted and honoured until the lobby is empty.

---- MODULE W4Od1m9p4t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Aircraft, MinCap, MaxCap, MaxEpoch

\* status: where each aircraft stands; stamp: the epoch its clearance carries;
\* declared: the capacity the supervisor has published for the current epoch.
VARIABLES status, stamp, epoch, declared

vars == <<status, stamp, epoch, declared>>

States == {"holding", "cleared", "onfield"}

TypeOK ==
    /\ status \in [Aircraft -> States]
    /\ stamp \in [Aircraft -> 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ declared \in MinCap..MaxCap

Init ==
    /\ status = [a \in Aircraft |-> "holding"]
    /\ stamp = [a \in Aircraft |-> 0]
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ declared = MinCap

\* A clearance counts against capacity only while its stamp is current.
Live(a) == status[a] = "cleared" /\ stamp[a] = epoch
OnField == {a \in Aircraft : status[a] = "onfield"}
Reserved == {a \in Aircraft : Live(a)}

Grant(a) ==
    /\ status[a] = "holding"
    /\ Cardinality(OnField) + Cardinality(Reserved) < declared
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![a] = "cleared"]
    /\ stamp' = [stamp EXCEPT ![a] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, declared>>

Roll(a) ==
    /\ Live(a)
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![a] = "onfield"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stamp, epoch, declared>>

Vacate(a) ==
    /\ status[a] = "onfield"
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![a] = "holding"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stamp, epoch, declared>>

\* The supervisor may not declare less room than the field already holds.
Redeclare ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ \E n \in MinCap..MaxCap :
        /\ n >= Cardinality(OnField)
        /\ declared' = n
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<status, stamp>>

\* A clearance sized against a superseded configuration is torn up.
Void(a) ==
    /\ status[a] = "cleared"
    /\ stamp[a] # epoch
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![a] = "holding"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stamp, epoch, declared>>

Next ==
    \/ \E a \in Aircraft : Grant(a) \/ Roll(a) \/ Vacate(a) \/ Void(a)
    \/ Redeclare

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

WithinDeclaredCapacity ==
    Cardinality(OnField) + Cardinality(Reserved) <= declared
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Aircraft = {ac1, ac2, ac3}
    MinCap = 1
    MaxCap = 2
    MaxEpoch = 2

INVARIANT WithinDeclaredCapacity
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator at a busy field decides how many aircraft may be on the movement area at once. The number is not fixed: crosswind, a closed taxiway, or a snow-removal crew can force the supervisor to redeclare the field's accepted capacity in the middle of a push, and the redeclaration can lower the number as well as raise it.

Every redeclaration opens a new configuration epoch, and the epoch counter is stamped onto everything the allocator issues. An aircraft in the holding stack that is granted permission to proceed receives a clearance stamped with the epoch that was current when the allocator granted it. That clearance counts against the field's capacity from the moment it is issued, not from the moment the aircraft actually rolls, because the allocator must reserve the room the aircraft will occupy. When the aircraft rolls onto the field it converts its clearance into occupancy and the stamp stops mattering.

A redeclaration invalidates every clearance that has not yet been converted, because those clearances were sized against the old configuration. An aircraft holding an out-of-epoch clearance is sent back to the holding stack and must be granted a fresh one. The supervisor is not permitted to redeclare a capacity smaller than the number of aircraft already physically on the field; aircraft already rolling cannot be un-cleared, so the new number must at least cover them.

The full set of actions is: Grant, in which the allocator issues an epoch-stamped clearance to an aircraft in the holding stack, but only while the aircraft already on the field plus the clearances still valid in the current epoch leave room under the declared capacity; Roll, in which an aircraft whose clearance carries the current epoch moves onto the field and becomes occupancy; Vacate, in which an aircraft on the field exits the movement area and rejoins the holding stack; Redeclare, in which the supervisor opens a new epoch and sets a new accepted capacity that is at least the number of aircraft currently on the field; and Void, in which an aircraft whose clearance carries a superseded epoch is sent back to the holding stack with its clearance torn up.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every instant the number of aircraft on the movement area, counted together with the clearances still valid in the current epoch, is no greater than the capacity the supervisor has declared for that epoch.

---- MODULE W4Od1m8p3t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Flights, Sectors, SlotsPerSector, NIL

\* A slot is named by its sector and its index within that sector.
Slots == [sec: Sectors, idx: 1..SlotsPerSector]
SectorOf(sl) == sl.sec

\* latch: coarse per-sector holder; board: the allocator's slot assignment;
\* held: the slot each flight believes is its own; snap: the free-slot snapshot
\* handed out with the coarse latch; pending: unordered request pool.
VARIABLES latch, board, held, snap, pending

vars == <<latch, board, held, snap, pending>>

Requests == [flight: Flights, sector: Sectors]

TypeOK ==
    /\ latch \in [Sectors -> Flights \cup {NIL}]
    /\ board \in [Slots -> Flights \cup {NIL}]
    /\ held \in [Flights -> Slots \cup {NIL}]
    /\ snap \in [Flights -> SUBSET Slots]
    /\ pending \subseteq Requests

Init ==
    /\ latch = [s \in Sectors |-> NIL]
    /\ board = [sl \in Slots |-> NIL]
    /\ held = [f \in Flights |-> NIL]
    /\ snap = [f \in Flights |-> {}]
    /\ pending = {}

Latched(f) == \E s \in Sectors : latch[s] = f
Filed(f) == \E r \in pending : r.flight = f

File(f, s) ==
    /\ held[f] = NIL /\ ~Filed(f) /\ ~Latched(f)
    /\ pending' = pending \cup {[flight |-> f, sector |-> s]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<latch, board, held, snap>>

FreeIn(s) == {sl \in Slots : SectorOf(sl) = s /\ board[sl] = NIL}

\* The coarse latch comes with a snapshot of what was free at that instant.
Latch(r) ==
    /\ r \in pending
    /\ latch[r.sector] = NIL
    /\ held[r.flight] = NIL
    /\ latch' = [latch EXCEPT ![r.sector] = r.flight]
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![r.flight] = FreeIn(r.sector)]
    /\ pending' = pending \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<board, held>>

\* The snapshot is trusted, not re-checked; the coarse latch is what keeps it true.
Take(f, sl) ==
    /\ latch[SectorOf(sl)] = f
    /\ sl \in snap[f]
    /\ held[f] = NIL
    /\ board' = [board EXCEPT ![sl] = f]
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![f] = sl]
    /\ latch' = [latch EXCEPT ![SectorOf(sl)] = NIL]
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![f] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED pending

Release(f) ==
    /\ held[f] # NIL
    /\ board' = [board EXCEPT ![held[f]] = NIL]
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![f] = NIL]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<latch, snap, pending>>

Refile(f, s) ==
    /\ latch[s] = f
    /\ snap[f] = {}
    /\ latch' = [latch EXCEPT ![s] = NIL]
    /\ pending' = pending \cup {[flight |-> f, sector |-> s]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<board, held, snap>>

TakeFor(f) == \E sl \in Slots : Take(f, sl)
RefileFor(f) == \E s \in Sectors : Refile(f, s)

Next ==
    \/ \E f \in Flights, s \in Sectors : File(f, s)
    \/ \E r \in pending : Latch(r)
    \/ \E f \in Flights : TakeFor(f) \/ RefileFor(f) \/ Release(f)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ \A f \in Flights : WF_vars(TakeFor(f)) /\ WF_vars(RefileFor(f))

BoardAgreesWithFlights ==
    \A f \in Flights : held[f] # NIL => board[held[f]] = f

LatchAlwaysReleased ==
    \A s \in Sectors : (latch[s] # NIL) ~> (latch[s] = NIL)
====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Flights = {ua11, dl22}
    Sectors = {north, south}
    SlotsPerSector = 2
    NIL = NIL

INVARIANT BoardAgreesWithFlights

PROPERTY LatchAlwaysReleased
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator hands departure slots to flights. Slots are grouped by sector, and the allocator protects them with a two-level scheme: a flight must first take the sector's coarse latch, and only then may it take a specific slot inside that sector. Taking the coarse latch is what lets a flight trust what it sees, because at the moment it takes the latch the allocator hands it a snapshot listing exactly which slots in that sector were unassigned. The flight then picks a slot out of that snapshot without re-checking the board; the whole point of the coarse latch is that nobody else can be picking in that sector at the same time, so the snapshot cannot go stale underneath it.

Slot requests reach the allocator over a datalink that does not preserve order. Requests sit in the allocator's pending pool and are picked up in whatever order the allocator gets to them, so a request filed later may well be latched earlier.

Taking a slot ends the coarse phase: as the flight records the slot as its own, it drops the sector latch so other flights can proceed. If the snapshot the flight received was empty, the sector was full when it latched, and the flight drops the latch and refiles its request into the pending pool to try again later. A flight that already holds a slot never files a new request and never takes a latch; it releases its slot when it departs, which returns the slot to the unassigned pool.

The full set of actions is: File, in which a flight with no slot and no request outstanding puts a request for a sector into the pending pool; Latch, in which the allocator picks any pending request whose sector is unlatched, gives that flight the coarse latch, and hands it a snapshot of the sector's currently unassigned slots; Take, in which a latched flight records one slot from its snapshot as its own and simultaneously drops the sector latch; Release, in which a flight holding a slot departs and returns the slot to the unassigned pool; and Refile, in which a latched flight whose snapshot is empty drops the latch and puts its request back into the pending pool.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a flight records a slot as its own, the allocator's board agrees that the slot belongs to that flight, so no slot is ever handed to two flights at once.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: A sector's coarse latch is never held forever — every latched sector eventually becomes unlatched again, because the latching flight must either take a slot or refile its request.

---- MODULE W4Od15m8p3t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Firms, Levels, NOBODY

\* bookLock: the coarse lock over the whole opening book.
\* slotOf: which firm currently holds each price level's crossing slot.
\* printing: which firm has actually started the cross at each level.
\* live: a crashed firm stops acting and says nothing; suspect: the
\* supervisor's unreliable guess about which firms are gone.
VARIABLES bookLock, slotOf, printing, live, suspect

vars == <<bookLock, slotOf, printing, live, suspect>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ bookLock \in Firms \cup {NOBODY}
    /\ slotOf \in [Levels -> Firms \cup {NOBODY}]
    /\ printing \in [Levels -> Firms \cup {NOBODY}]
    /\ live \in [Firms -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ suspect \subseteq Firms

Init ==
    /\ bookLock = NOBODY
    /\ slotOf = [l \in Levels |-> NOBODY]
    /\ printing = [l \in Levels |-> NOBODY]
    /\ live = [f \in Firms |-> TRUE]
    /\ suspect = {}

TakeBook(f) ==
    /\ live[f] /\ bookLock = NOBODY
    /\ bookLock' = f
    /\ UNCHANGED <<slotOf, printing, live, suspect>>

\* The coarse lock is dropped in the same step that the fine slot is taken.
TakeLevel(f, l) ==
    /\ live[f] /\ bookLock = f /\ slotOf[l] = NOBODY
    /\ slotOf' = [slotOf EXCEPT ![l] = f]
    /\ bookLock' = NOBODY
    /\ UNCHANGED <<printing, live, suspect>>

Execute(f, l) ==
    /\ live[f] /\ slotOf[l] = f /\ printing[l] = NOBODY
    /\ printing' = [printing EXCEPT ![l] = f]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bookLock, slotOf, live, suspect>>

Print(f, l) ==
    /\ live[f] /\ printing[l] = f
    /\ printing' = [printing EXCEPT ![l] = NOBODY]
    /\ slotOf' = [slotOf EXCEPT ![l] = NOBODY]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bookLock, live, suspect>>

Crash(f) ==
    /\ live[f]
    /\ live' = [live EXCEPT ![f] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bookLock, slotOf, printing, suspect>>

Reconnect(f) ==
    /\ ~live[f]
    /\ live' = [live EXCEPT ![f] = TRUE]
    /\ suspect' = suspect \ {f}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bookLock, slotOf, printing>>

Suspect(f) ==
    /\ f \notin suspect
    /\ suspect' = suspect \cup {f}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bookLock, slotOf, printing, live>>

PullBook(f) ==
    /\ bookLock = f /\ f \in suspect
    /\ bookLock' = NOBODY
    /\ UNCHANGED <<slotOf, printing, live, suspect>>

\* Suspicion is never enough to pull a level that is already crossing.
PullLevel(f, l) ==
    /\ slotOf[l] = f /\ f \in suspect /\ printing[l] = NOBODY
    /\ slotOf' = [slotOf EXCEPT ![l] = NOBODY]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bookLock, printing, live, suspect>>

Next ==
    \/ \E f \in Firms : TakeBook(f) \/ Crash(f) \/ Reconnect(f)
                        \/ Suspect(f) \/ PullBook(f)
    \/ \E f \in Firms, l \in Levels :
        TakeLevel(f, l) \/ Execute(f, l) \/ Print(f, l) \/ PullLevel(f, l)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CrossingFirmStillHoldsSlot ==
    \A l \in Levels : printing[l] # NOBODY => slotOf[l] = printing[l]
====
nl:
A stock exchange runs an opening auction. Each price level in the opening book has exactly one crossing slot, and a member firm that wants to cross at a level must first be granted that level's slot. Because the book is rebuilt continuously right up to the cross, the exchange guards it with two nested locks: a member must first take the whole-book lock, and only while holding it may it take the slot at a single price level. Taking the level slot immediately releases the book lock, so the coarse lock is held only for the instant it takes to pick a level.

Once a firm holds a level's slot it may begin executing at that level, which is the irreversible part: matching engines start printing the cross. Executing finishes by printing the last lot, which both ends the execution and returns the level's slot to the exchange for the next auction phase.

Member firms can crash silently. A crashed firm stops taking locks, stops executing, and sends no notice; the exchange learns nothing directly. What the exchange has instead is a supervisor that may declare any member suspect at any time, on nothing more than a hunch about latency. Once a member is suspect the supervisor may pull back the book lock it holds, and may pull back a level slot it holds — but only a level slot at which the member has not started executing. A level with an execution in progress is never pulled back on suspicion alone, because the supervisor cannot tell a slow firm from a dead one and printing the same level twice would be a market-integrity failure. A firm that was wrongly declared suspect can come back: it reconnects, the supervisor clears the suspicion, and it resumes.

The full set of actions is: TakeBook, in which a live member takes the free book lock; TakeLevel, in which the member holding the book lock takes a free level slot and drops the book lock in the same step; Execute, in which a live member that holds a level slot begins executing at that level; Print, in which a live executing member finishes the cross, ending the execution and returning the level slot; Crash, in which a live member silently stops; Reconnect, in which a crashed member comes back alive and is no longer suspect; Suspect, in which the supervisor declares a member suspect; PullBook, in which the supervisor takes the book lock back from a suspect member; and PullLevel, in which the supervisor takes a level slot back from a suspect member that has not started executing at that level.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A member is executing at a price level only while that level's slot is still granted to that same member, so the exchange never has one firm printing a level whose slot has been handed elsewhere.

---- MODULE W4Od3m4p0t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Batches, MinDepth, MaxDepth, IDLE

\* window: the one batch the posting engine currently has open, if any.
\* depth: the intake queue's admission limit, retuned by the ops desk.
VARIABLES queue, state, window, depth

vars == <<queue, state, window, depth>>

Stages == {"fresh", "queued", "posting", "posted", "refused"}

TypeOK ==
    /\ queue \in Seq(Batches)
    /\ state \in [Batches -> Stages]
    /\ window \in Batches \cup {IDLE}
    /\ depth \in MinDepth..MaxDepth

Init ==
    /\ queue = <<>>
    /\ state = [b \in Batches |-> "fresh"]
    /\ window = IDLE
    /\ depth = MinDepth

Admit(b) ==
    /\ state[b] = "fresh"
    /\ Len(queue) < depth
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, b)
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![b] = "queued"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<window, depth>>

\* Backpressure: at the limit the batch is refused, never quietly buffered.
Refuse(b) ==
    /\ state[b] = "fresh"
    /\ Len(queue) >= depth
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![b] = "refused"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, window, depth>>

Represent(b) ==
    /\ state[b] = "refused"
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![b] = "fresh"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, window, depth>>

\* The engine takes strictly the oldest queued batch, so nobody is overtaken.
Begin ==
    /\ window = IDLE
    /\ queue # <<>>
    /\ window' = Head(queue)
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![Head(queue)] = "posting"]
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED depth

Complete ==
    /\ window # IDLE
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![window] = "posted"]
    /\ window' = IDLE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, depth>>

Retune ==
    /\ \E n \in MinDepth..MaxDepth : depth' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, state, window>>

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Batches : Admit(b) \/ Refuse(b) \/ Represent(b)
    \/ Begin \/ Complete \/ Retune

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Begin) /\ WF_vars(Complete)

PostingIsTheOpenWindow ==
    \A b \in Batches : state[b] = "posting" => window = b

AdmittedBatchesGetPosted ==
    \A b \in Batches : (state[b] = "queued") ~> (state[b] = "posted")
====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Batches = {b1, b2, b3}
    MinDepth = 1
    MaxDepth = 2
    IDLE = IDLE

INVARIANT PostingIsTheOpenWindow

PROPERTY AdmittedBatchesGetPosted
nl:
A clearing bank posts interbank settlement batches through a single posting engine. The engine is the critical resource: it holds the ledger open, applies a batch's debits and credits, and closes the ledger again, and it can only ever be working one batch at a time. A batch that is being posted is said to be in the window, and the engine records which batch is in its window.

Batches do not go straight to the engine. They are admitted into a bounded intake queue and posted strictly in the order they were admitted, oldest first, so an older batch is never overtaken by a newer one. The queue's admission depth is a live operational parameter: the operations desk raises it when the correspondent banks are sending heavily and lowers it when the ledger is running close to its cut-off, and the change takes effect on the next admission decision.

Backpressure is explicit rather than silent. When a batch is presented and the queue already holds as many batches as the current admission depth allows, the batch is refused outright rather than buffered, and the submitting desk is told so. A refused batch is not lost: the desk can present it again later, when the depth may have been raised or the queue may have drained.

The full set of actions is: Admit, in which a freshly presented batch is placed at the back of the intake queue because the queue is below the current admission depth; Refuse, in which a freshly presented batch is rejected because the queue is already at the current admission depth; Represent, in which a refused batch is presented again as fresh; Begin, in which the idle engine takes the oldest queued batch into its window and starts posting it; Complete, in which the engine finishes the batch in its window, marks it posted, and goes idle again; and Retune, in which the operations desk changes the queue's admission depth to any value in the supported range.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A batch is in the posting state only when it is the batch the engine is holding in its window, so two batches are never posting against the ledger at the same time.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every batch that is admitted to the intake queue is eventually posted, because the engine keeps taking the oldest queued batch and finishing it.

---- MODULE W4Od6m5p2t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Controllers, Banks, TotalUnits, Quorum, NOPROP

\* pool: spare drives in the machine room; installed: drives fitted per bank;
\* staged: drives already pulled from the pool for the open proposal.
VARIABLES pool, installed, open, tally, staged

vars == <<pool, installed, open, tally, staged>>

Proposals == [bank: Banks, units: 1..TotalUnits]

TypeOK ==
    /\ pool \in 0..TotalUnits
    /\ installed \in [Banks -> 0..TotalUnits]
    /\ open \in Proposals \cup {NOPROP}
    /\ tally \subseteq Controllers
    /\ staged \in 0..TotalUnits

Init ==
    /\ pool = TotalUnits
    /\ installed = [b \in Banks |-> 0]
    /\ open = NOPROP
    /\ tally = {}
    /\ staged = 0

\* Filing takes the units out of the pool at once, so no second proposal can
\* be written against drives this one has already spoken for.
File(b, n) ==
    /\ open = NOPROP
    /\ n <= pool
    /\ open' = [bank |-> b, units |-> n]
    /\ pool' = pool - n
    /\ staged' = n
    /\ tally' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED installed

Vote(c) ==
    /\ open # NOPROP
    /\ c \notin tally
    /\ tally' = tally \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, installed, open, staged>>

Commit ==
    /\ open # NOPROP
    /\ Cardinality(tally) >= Quorum
    /\ installed' = [installed EXCEPT ![open.bank] = @ + staged]
    /\ staged' = 0
    /\ open' = NOPROP
    /\ tally' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED pool

Withdraw ==
    /\ open # NOPROP
    /\ Cardinality(tally) < Quorum
    /\ pool' = pool + staged
    /\ staged' = 0
    /\ open' = NOPROP
    /\ tally' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED installed

Return(b, n) ==
    /\ open = NOPROP
    /\ n <= installed[b]
    /\ installed' = [installed EXCEPT ![b] = @ - n]
    /\ pool' = pool + n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<open, tally, staged>>

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Banks, n \in 1..TotalUnits : File(b, n) \/ Return(b, n)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Vote(c)
    \/ Commit \/ Withdraw

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

Fitted == LET Sum[S \in SUBSET Banks] ==
                IF S = {} THEN 0
                ELSE LET b == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE
                     IN installed[b] + Sum[S \ {b}]
          IN Sum[Banks]

DrivesAreConserved == pool + Fitted + staged = TotalUnits
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Controllers = {c1, c2, c3}
    Banks = {lowRise, highRise}
    TotalUnits = 3
    Quorum = 2
    NOPROP = NOPROP

INVARIANT DrivesAreConserved
nl:
A skyscraper is served by two independent elevator banks, a low-rise bank and a high-rise bank, each with its own dispatcher and its own schedule. What they are not independent about is standby hoist drives: the building keeps one shared pool of spare drive units in the machine room, and either bank can draw units out of that pool to bring extra cars into service. Drive units are physical objects. The building's engineer accounts for every one of them, and the total number in the building never changes on its own — a unit is either sitting in the pool, installed in one of the two banks, or in the middle of being moved.

Because the two banks would otherwise race each other for the same units, no bank may take units on its own authority. Each transfer is put to a panel of building controllers and needs a quorum of them to approve. A proposal names one bank and a number of units, and the units it asks for are pulled out of the pool the instant the proposal is filed and set aside in a staging cage, so that a second proposal cannot be written against units the first has already spoken for. Controllers then vote one at a time. When enough controllers have voted to reach quorum, the proposal commits: the staged units are installed in the named bank and the staging cage is emptied. A proposal that has not reached quorum may instead be withdrawn, in which case the staged units go straight back into the pool. Only one proposal is ever open at a time.

Units also come back. When a bank takes a car out of service it returns drive units to the pool directly, which needs no vote, but it may only do so while no proposal is open.

The full set of actions is: File, in which a proposal for a bank and a number of units is opened, the units are moved from the pool into the staging cage, and the vote tally is cleared; Vote, in which one controller that has not yet voted adds its vote to the open proposal; Commit, in which a proposal that has reached quorum installs its staged units into the named bank and closes; Withdraw, in which an open proposal that has not reached quorum is closed and its staged units are returned to the pool; and Return, in which a bank hands units back into the pool while no proposal is open.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of drive units in the pool, plus those installed across both banks, plus those sitting in the staging cage, is always exactly the number of units the building owns.

---- MODULE W4Od10m5p5t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Nodes, Trains, Quorum, MaxRound, NONE

\* open: the highest round opened so far (0 = none yet).
\* named: each round's candidate train; ballot: who has voted in each round.
\* carried: the rounds that reached quorum and cleared the signal.
VARIABLES open, named, ballot, carried, up

vars == <<open, named, ballot, carried, up>>

Rounds == 1..MaxRound

TypeOK ==
    /\ open \in 0..MaxRound
    /\ named \in [Rounds -> Trains \cup {NONE}]
    /\ ballot \in [Rounds -> SUBSET Nodes]
    /\ carried \subseteq Rounds
    /\ up \in [Nodes -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
    /\ open = 0
    /\ named = [r \in Rounds |-> NONE]
    /\ ballot = [r \in Rounds |-> {}]
    /\ carried = {}
    /\ up = [n \in Nodes |-> TRUE]

\* Carry-over: once some round has carried, later rounds may name only its train.
Permitted(t) == \A r \in carried : named[r] = t

Open(t) ==
    /\ open < MaxRound
    /\ Permitted(t)
    /\ open' = open + 1
    /\ named' = [named EXCEPT ![open + 1] = t]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, carried, up>>

Vote(n) ==
    /\ up[n]
    /\ open \in Rounds
    /\ open \notin carried
    /\ n \notin ballot[open]
    /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![open] = @ \cup {n}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<open, named, carried, up>>

Carry ==
    /\ open \in Rounds
    /\ open \notin carried
    /\ Cardinality(ballot[open]) >= Quorum
    /\ carried' = carried \cup {open}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<open, named, ballot, up>>

\* At most one node is ever down, so a quorum of the rest stays reachable.
Crash(n) ==
    /\ \A m \in Nodes : up[m]
    /\ up' = [up EXCEPT ![n] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<open, named, ballot, carried>>

Restore(n) ==
    /\ ~up[n]
    /\ up' = [up EXCEPT ![n] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<open, named, ballot, carried>>

OpenStep == \E t \in Trains : Open(t)
VoteStep == \E n \in Nodes : Vote(n)

Next ==
    \/ OpenStep
    \/ VoteStep
    \/ Carry
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Crash(n) \/ Restore(n)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(OpenStep)
        /\ WF_vars(VoteStep) /\ WF_vars(Carry)

CarriedRoundsAgree ==
    \A r1, r2 \in carried : named[r1] = named[r2]

AuthorityIsEventuallyGranted == <>(carried # {})
====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Nodes = {ixA, ixB, ixC}
    Trains = {t101, t202}
    Quorum = 2
    MaxRound = 2
    NONE = NONE

INVARIANT CarriedRoundsAgree

PROPERTY AuthorityIsEventuallyGranted
nl:
A subway signalling system must decide which train is given the movement authority for a particular track block. Handing out that authority is irreversible: the signal clears, the train commits to the block at line speed, and nothing the interlocking does afterwards can take it back. The decision is therefore not made by any single signalling node. It is made by a panel of interlocking nodes voting in numbered rounds, and a round only takes effect once a quorum of nodes has voted in it.

A round is opened by naming one train as that round's candidate. Rounds are opened one at a time and numbered in order. The rule that keeps the system honest is the carry-over rule: if any earlier round has already carried, a newly opened round is not free to name a different train — it must name the train that carried. Only when no round has carried yet is the choice open.

Nodes vote for the candidate of the round that is currently open, one vote per node per round, and only while that round has not yet carried. When the votes in the open round reach quorum, the round carries and the signal clears for that round's candidate.

One node can crash silently. It stops voting and gives no notice; the rest of the panel cannot distinguish it from a slow node, which is why the quorum is set below the panel size. A crashed node can later be restored by a technician on site, at which point it resumes voting. At most one node is ever down at a time, so a quorum of the remaining nodes is always reachable.

The full set of actions is: Open, in which the next round is opened naming a candidate train, subject to the carry-over rule; Vote, in which a live node casts its vote in the open round; Carry, in which the open round reaches quorum and carries, clearing the signal for its candidate; Crash, in which a node silently stops while every other node is still up; and Restore, in which the crashed node is brought back and resumes voting.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any two rounds that have carried name the same train, so the block's movement authority is never irreversibly granted to two different trains.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Some round eventually carries, so the block's authority is eventually granted rather than left undecided.

---- MODULE W4Od0m7p1t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Teams, MaxRooms, MinOpen, MaxLog, NODRAFT

Rooms == 1..MaxRooms

\* journal: the append-only revision log for the whole day.
\* reg: each room's compare-and-swap register, counting its entries.
\* draft: the pending read-modify-write each team is carrying.
\* openRooms: how many rooms theatre management has staffed right now.
VARIABLES journal, reg, draft, openRooms

vars == <<journal, reg, draft, openRooms>>

Entries == [team: Teams, room: Rooms, base: 0..MaxLog]

TypeOK ==
    /\ journal \in Seq(Entries)
    /\ reg \in [Rooms -> 0..MaxLog]
    /\ draft \in [Teams -> ([room: Rooms, base: 0..MaxLog] \cup {NODRAFT})]
    /\ openRooms \in MinOpen..MaxRooms

Init ==
    /\ journal = <<>>
    /\ reg = [r \in Rooms |-> 0]
    /\ draft = [t \in Teams |-> NODRAFT]
    /\ openRooms = MinOpen

Read(t, r) ==
    /\ draft[t] = NODRAFT
    /\ r <= openRooms
    /\ draft' = [draft EXCEPT ![t] = [room |-> r, base |-> reg[r]]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<journal, reg, openRooms>>

\* The swap lands only if the register still holds what the draft read.
Swap(t) ==
    /\ draft[t] # NODRAFT
    /\ Len(journal) < MaxLog
    /\ reg[draft[t].room] = draft[t].base
    /\ journal' = Append(journal, [team |-> t, room |-> draft[t].room,
                                   base |-> draft[t].base])
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![draft[t].room] = @ + 1]
    /\ draft' = [draft EXCEPT ![t] = NODRAFT]
    /\ UNCHANGED openRooms

Refuse(t) ==
    /\ draft[t] # NODRAFT
    /\ reg[draft[t].room] # draft[t].base
    /\ draft' = [draft EXCEPT ![t] = NODRAFT]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<journal, reg, openRooms>>

Abandon(t) ==
    /\ draft[t] # NODRAFT
    /\ draft[t].room > openRooms
    /\ draft' = [draft EXCEPT ![t] = NODRAFT]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<journal, reg, openRooms>>

Staff ==
    /\ \E n \in MinOpen..MaxRooms : openRooms' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<journal, reg, draft>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Teams, r \in Rooms : Read(t, r)
    \/ \E t \in Teams : Swap(t) \/ Refuse(t) \/ Abandon(t)
    \/ Staff

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

EarlierFor(i) ==
    Cardinality({j \in 1..(i - 1) : journal[j].room = journal[i].room})

\* Every entry was built on exactly the room history that preceded it.
JournalIsContiguousPerRoom ==
    \A i \in 1..Len(journal) : journal[i].base = EarlierFor(i)
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Teams = {orthoTeam, cardioTeam}
    MaxRooms = 2
    MinOpen = 1
    MaxLog = 3
    NODRAFT = NODRAFT

INVARIANT JournalIsContiguousPerRoom
nl:
A hospital keeps one shared operating-room day plan. The plan is not stored as a table that people overwrite; it is stored as an append-only revision journal, one entry per booking change, and every entry records which surgical team made the change, which room it concerns, and how many earlier entries that team believed already existed for that room. That last number is the whole point: a team must state what it thought it was building on.

Each room exposes a small compare-and-swap register holding the count of journal entries written for that room so far. Booking is a read-modify-write: a team first reads a room's register and prepares a draft change carrying the count it read; later it tries to swap the draft into the journal. The swap goes through only if the room's register still holds the count the draft was prepared against. If it does, the entry is appended and the room's register advances by one. If another team has booked that room in the meantime, the register has moved, the swap is refused, and the team throws the draft away and starts over from a fresh read.

The number of rooms actually open changes during the day. Theatre management opens or closes rooms as anaesthetic staff arrive or are pulled to emergencies, and the change takes effect immediately. A team may only read a register for a room that is currently open, and a team holding a draft for a room that has since been closed abandons that draft. A team holds at most one draft at a time. The journal for the day has a fixed maximum length; once it is full no further entries are appended.

The full set of actions is: Read, in which a team with no draft in hand reads an open room's register and prepares a draft carrying the count it read; Swap, in which a team's draft is appended to the journal because the room's register still matches the draft's count, advancing that register; Refuse, in which a team's draft is discarded because the room's register no longer matches; Abandon, in which a team discards a draft for a room that management has since closed; and Staff, in which management changes how many rooms are open.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every entry in the journal, the count the entry was built on is exactly the number of earlier journal entries for that same room, so no booking change is ever written on top of a room state it did not actually see.

---- MODULE W4Od15m6p0t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Nodes

\* leased: who currently holds a lease on the cross engine.
\* beat: whether the holder has heartbeated inside the open renewal window.
\* bids: the registrar's unordered request set; onEngine: who is driving.
VARIABLES leased, beat, bids, onEngine, printed

vars == <<leased, beat, bids, onEngine, printed>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ leased \in [Nodes -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ beat \in [Nodes -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ bids \subseteq Nodes
    /\ onEngine \subseteq Nodes
    /\ printed \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
    /\ leased = [n \in Nodes |-> FALSE]
    /\ beat = [n \in Nodes |-> FALSE]
    /\ bids = {}
    /\ onEngine = {}
    /\ printed = FALSE

Bid(n) ==
    /\ ~leased[n] /\ n \notin bids
    /\ bids' = bids \cup {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leased, beat, onEngine, printed>>

\* The registrar serves the request set in no particular order.
Grant(n) ==
    /\ n \in bids
    /\ \A m \in Nodes : ~leased[m]
    /\ leased' = [leased EXCEPT ![n] = TRUE]
    /\ beat' = [beat EXCEPT ![n] = TRUE]
    /\ bids' = bids \ {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onEngine, printed>>

Renew(n) ==
    /\ leased[n] /\ ~beat[n]
    /\ beat' = [beat EXCEPT ![n] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leased, bids, onEngine, printed>>

Lapse(n) ==
    /\ leased[n] /\ beat[n]
    /\ beat' = [beat EXCEPT ![n] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leased, bids, onEngine, printed>>

Mount(n) ==
    /\ leased[n] /\ n \notin onEngine
    /\ onEngine' = onEngine \cup {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leased, beat, bids, printed>>

Print(n) ==
    /\ n \in onEngine /\ leased[n]
    /\ printed' = TRUE
    /\ onEngine' = onEngine \ {n}
    /\ leased' = [leased EXCEPT ![n] = FALSE]
    /\ beat' = [beat EXCEPT ![n] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED bids

\* Reclaiming the lease removes the holder from the engine in the same step.
Expire(n) ==
    /\ leased[n] /\ ~beat[n]
    /\ leased' = [leased EXCEPT ![n] = FALSE]
    /\ onEngine' = onEngine \ {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<beat, bids, printed>>

BidStep == \E n \in Nodes : Bid(n)
GrantStep == \E n \in Nodes : Grant(n)
MountStep == \E n \in Nodes : Mount(n)
PrintStep == \E n \in Nodes : Print(n)

Next ==
    \/ BidStep \/ GrantStep \/ MountStep \/ PrintStep
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Renew(n) \/ Lapse(n) \/ Expire(n)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ WF_vars(BidStep) /\ WF_vars(GrantStep)
        /\ SF_vars(MountStep) /\ SF_vars(PrintStep)

OnEngineOnlyUnderLease == \A n \in onEngine : leased[n]

CrossIsEventuallyPrinted == <>printed
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Nodes = {matchA, matchB}

INVARIANT OnEngineOnlyUnderLease

PROPERTY CrossIsEventuallyPrinted
nl:
A stock exchange runs its opening auction on a cross engine that must be driven by exactly one matching node. Driving the engine is the critical section: while a node is on the engine it is computing and printing the opening price, and a second node computing at the same time would produce two different opening prints for the same symbol.

Ownership of the engine is handed out as a lease rather than as a permanent assignment, because a matching node can go quiet without warning and the auction cannot wait for it. Nodes that want the engine put a bid for it into the registrar's request set. That set has no order to it — bids arrive over an unordered fabric, and the registrar picks whichever bid it happens to look at first, so a bid filed earlier may well be served later. The registrar grants a lease only when no lease is outstanding.

A lease is kept alive by heartbeats. The holder must renew within each renewal window; the window then lapses and must be renewed again. If the window lapses and the holder has not renewed, the registrar expires the lease, and expiring a lease also takes its holder off the cross engine in the same instant — that is what makes it safe to hand the engine to somebody else. A node steps onto the engine only while it actually holds a live lease, and it prints the opening cross from the engine, which ends its turn and gives the lease back.

The full set of actions is: Bid, in which a node without a lease adds itself to the registrar's unordered request set; Grant, in which the registrar picks any bid from that set and gives that node a lease, provided no lease is currently outstanding; Renew, in which the holder of a lease sends its heartbeat for the current renewal window; Lapse, in which the current renewal window closes and the heartbeat must be sent again; Mount, in which a node holding a live lease steps onto the cross engine; Print, in which a node on the engine computes and prints the opening cross, then steps off and gives up its lease; and Expire, in which the registrar reclaims a lease whose renewal window lapsed without a heartbeat, removing its holder from the engine at the same moment.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every node standing on the cross engine holds a live lease at that moment, and since the registrar never grants a second lease while one is outstanding, two nodes are never on the engine together.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The opening cross is eventually printed, because leases keep being granted and a node that holds one repeatedly gets the chance to mount the engine and print.

---- MODULE W4Od0m7p6t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Surgeons, Rooms, MaxEpoch, NONE

\* attending: who may write against each room; era: the room's credential
\* epoch, bumped on every change of attending; badge: the credential a
\* surgeon is carrying; lastOrder: the most recent order written per room.
VARIABLES attending, era, badge, lastOrder, up

vars == <<attending, era, badge, lastOrder, up>>

Badges == [room: Rooms, era: 0..MaxEpoch]
Orders == [by: Surgeons, era: 0..MaxEpoch]

TypeOK ==
    /\ attending \in [Rooms -> Surgeons \cup {NONE}]
    /\ era \in [Rooms -> 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ badge \in [Surgeons -> Badges \cup {NONE}]
    /\ lastOrder \in [Rooms -> Orders \cup {NONE}]
    /\ up \in [Surgeons -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
    /\ attending = [r \in Rooms |-> NONE]
    /\ era = [r \in Rooms |-> 0]
    /\ badge = [s \in Surgeons |-> NONE]
    /\ lastOrder = [r \in Rooms |-> NONE]
    /\ up = [s \in Surgeons |-> TRUE]

Assign(s, r) ==
    /\ up[s] /\ attending[r] = NONE /\ era[r] < MaxEpoch
    /\ attending' = [attending EXCEPT ![r] = s]
    /\ era' = [era EXCEPT ![r] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<badge, lastOrder, up>>

Badge(s, r) ==
    /\ up[s] /\ attending[r] = s /\ badge[s] = NONE
    /\ badge' = [badge EXCEPT ![s] = [room |-> r, era |-> era[r]]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<attending, era, lastOrder, up>>

\* The write is admitted only on a badge whose epoch still matches the room.
Order(s) ==
    /\ up[s] /\ badge[s] # NONE
    /\ era[badge[s].room] = badge[s].era
    /\ attending[badge[s].room] = s
    /\ lastOrder' = [lastOrder EXCEPT ![badge[s].room] =
                        [by |-> s, era |-> era[badge[s].room]]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<attending, era, badge, up>>

Discard(s) ==
    /\ badge[s] # NONE
    /\ era[badge[s].room] # badge[s].era
    /\ badge' = [badge EXCEPT ![s] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<attending, era, lastOrder, up>>

\* The scheduler cannot see a silent surgeon, so it may stand any of them down.
Standdown(r) ==
    /\ attending[r] # NONE /\ era[r] < MaxEpoch
    /\ attending' = [attending EXCEPT ![r] = NONE]
    /\ era' = [era EXCEPT ![r] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<badge, lastOrder, up>>

Crash(s) ==
    /\ \A t \in Surgeons : up[t]
    /\ up' = [up EXCEPT ![s] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<attending, era, badge, lastOrder>>

Return(s) ==
    /\ ~up[s]
    /\ up' = [up EXCEPT ![s] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<attending, era, badge, lastOrder>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Surgeons, r \in Rooms : Assign(s, r) \/ Badge(s, r)
    \/ \E s \in Surgeons : Order(s) \/ Discard(s) \/ Crash(s) \/ Return(s)
    \/ \E r \in Rooms : Standdown(r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

StandingOrderIsAuthorised ==
    \A r \in Rooms :

====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Surgeons = {drAvery, drBoone}
    Rooms = {or1, or2}
    MaxEpoch = 2
    NONE = NONE

INVARIANT StandingOrderIsAuthorised
nl:
A hospital's operating-room scheduler decides who is allowed to write orders against each room. Each room has exactly one attending surgeon at a time, and the room's record carries a credential epoch that is bumped every time the attending changes — both when a surgeon is put on the room and when one is taken off it. The epoch is held in a small compare-and-swap register on the room, and it is the only thing that distinguishes a current credential from one that has been superseded.

A surgeon who is put on a room draws a badge from that room: the badge records the room and the epoch that was current when the badge was drawn. A surgeon carries at most one badge. To write an order the surgeon presents its badge, and the write goes through only if the epoch on the badge still equals the epoch in the room's register and the surgeon is still the room named on the record. If the epoch has moved on, the badge is worthless and the surgeon discards it and must be re-badged. Each order that is written is stamped with the room's epoch as it stood at the moment of the write, together with the surgeon who wrote it; the room keeps the most recent order written against it.

Surgeons can go silent. A surgeon may crash — scrubbed out, paged away, radio dead — and simply stop acting, with no notice to the scheduler. The scheduler cannot see this, so what it has instead is the ability to take any surgeon off a room at any time, which bumps that room's epoch and immediately invalidates every badge drawn against it. A surgeon who went silent can be brought back later. At most one surgeon is out at a time.

The full set of actions is: Assign, in which a live surgeon is made the attending on a room that currently has none, bumping the room's epoch; Badge, in which a live attending surgeon with no badge draws one from its room, recording the room's current epoch; Order, in which a live surgeon presents a badge whose epoch still matches the room and is still the room's attending, writing an order stamped with the surgeon and the room's current epoch; Discard, in which a surgeon throws away a badge whose epoch no longer matches the room; Standdown, in which the scheduler takes the attending off a room, bumping its epoch; Crash, in which a live surgeon silently stops while every other surgeon is up; and Return, in which the surgeon who was out comes back.

SAFETY PROPERTY: If the order most recently written against a room still carries that room's current epoch, then the surgeon who wrote it is still that room's attending, so no order standing at the current epoch was written by anybody unauthorised or working from a superseded credential.

---- MODULE W4Od8m6p3t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Students, SeatCount, MinOpen, MaxGen, NONE

Seats == 1..SeatCount

\* holder: who currently has an unconfirmed hold on each seat.
\* gen: the seat's hold generation, advanced on every hold and every lapse.
\* receipt: what the student is carrying; filled: confirmed enrollments.
VARIABLES holder, gen, receipt, filled, openSeats

vars == <<holder, gen, receipt, filled, openSeats>>

Receipts == [seat: Seats, gen: 0..MaxGen]
Fills == [who: Students, gen: 0..MaxGen]

TypeOK ==
    /\ holder \in [Seats -> Students \cup {NONE}]
    /\ gen \in [Seats -> 0..MaxGen]
    /\ receipt \in [Students -> Receipts \cup {NONE}]
    /\ filled \in [Seats -> Fills \cup {NONE}]
    /\ openSeats \in MinOpen..SeatCount

Init ==
    /\ holder = [s \in Seats |-> NONE]
    /\ gen = [s \in Seats |-> 0]
    /\ receipt = [st \in Students |-> NONE]
    /\ filled = [s \in Seats |-> NONE]
    /\ openSeats = MinOpen

Hold(st, s) ==
    /\ receipt[st] = NONE
    /\ s <= openSeats /\ holder[s] = NONE /\ filled[s] = NONE
    /\ gen[s] < MaxGen
    /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![s] = st]
    /\ gen' = [gen EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
    /\ receipt' = [receipt EXCEPT ![st] = [seat |-> s, gen |-> gen[s] + 1]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<filled, openSeats>>

\* The receipt is honoured only at the generation it was issued against.
Confirm(st) ==
    /\ receipt[st] # NONE
    /\ LET rc == receipt[st] IN
        /\ rc.seat <= openSeats
        /\ holder[rc.seat] = st
        /\ gen[rc.seat] = rc.gen
        /\ filled' = [filled EXCEPT ![rc.seat] = [who |-> st, gen |-> rc.gen]]
    /\ receipt' = [receipt EXCEPT ![st] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, gen, openSeats>>

\* A confirmed seat has left the lease system, so its hold never lapses.
Lapse(s) ==
    /\ holder[s] # NONE /\ filled[s] = NONE
    /\ gen[s] < MaxGen
    /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![s] = NONE]
    /\ gen' = [gen EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<receipt, filled, openSeats>>

Tear(st) ==
    /\ receipt[st] # NONE
    /\ \/ gen[receipt[st].seat] # receipt[st].gen
       \/ holder[receipt[st].seat] # st
       \/ receipt[st].seat > openSeats
    /\ receipt' = [receipt EXCEPT ![st] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, gen, filled, openSeats>>

Resize ==
    /\ \E n \in MinOpen..SeatCount :
        /\ \A s \in Seats : filled[s] # NONE => s <= n
        /\ openSeats' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, gen, receipt, filled>>

HoldStep == \E st \in Students, s \in Seats : Hold(st, s)
ConfirmStep == \E st \in Students : Confirm(st)
TearStep == \E st \in Students : Tear(st)

Next == HoldStep \/ ConfirmStep \/ Resize
        \/ \E s \in Seats : Lapse(s)
        \/ TearStep

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ WF_vars(HoldStep) /\ WF_vars(TearStep) /\ SF_vars(ConfirmStep)

ConfirmedSeatMatchesItsHold ==
    \A s \in Seats :
        filled[s] # NONE =>
            /\ holder[s] = filled[s].who
            /\ gen[s] = filled[s].gen

NoReceiptIsHeldForever ==
    \A st \in Students : (receipt[st] # NONE) ~> (receipt[st] = NONE)
====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Students = {sAmara, sBrix}
    SeatCount = 2
    MinOpen = 1
    MaxGen = 2
    NONE = NONE

INVARIANT ConfirmedSeatMatchesItsHold

PROPERTY NoReceiptIsHeldForever
nl:
A university course-registration system allocates the individual seats of a lab section. A seat is not handed over the moment a student clicks; the student is first given a registration hold on that seat, which is a lease. The hold gives the student a window in which to finish the paperwork, and it lapses on its own if the student walks away, so an abandoned cart does not sterilise a seat for the rest of the add period.

Every seat carries a hold generation. The generation advances each time a hold is placed on the seat and again each time a hold lapses, and the receipt the student is given records the seat together with the generation that was current when the hold was placed. Finishing registration means presenting that receipt: the registrar accepts it only if the seat's generation still matches the receipt and the seat is still recorded as held by that same student. If the generation has moved on, the receipt is worthless and the student throws it away and starts over. A student carries at most one receipt at a time. Once a seat is confirmed it is out of the lease system entirely: its hold no longer lapses and it cannot be re-held.

The section's size is not fixed. The department raises and lowers the number of open seats during the add period as room assignments and teaching-assistant coverage change. Only open seats can be held or confirmed, and a seat that is closed while merely held simply has its hold lapse. The department may not shrink the section below a seat that is already confirmed, because a confirmed student cannot be unenrolled by a room change.

The full set of actions is: Hold, in which a student with no receipt is given a hold on an open, unheld, unconfirmed seat, advancing that seat's generation and issuing a receipt; Confirm, in which a student presents a receipt whose generation still matches its open seat and is still that seat's holder, turning the hold into a confirmed enrollment and consuming the receipt; Lapse, in which a seat's unconfirmed hold expires, clearing the holder and advancing the generation; Tear, in which a student throws away a receipt whose seat has moved on to a later generation, is no longer held by that student, or has since been closed by the department; and Resize, in which the department sets the number of open seats to any supported value that still covers every confirmed seat.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every confirmed seat is still recorded as held by the very student who confirmed it, at the very generation that student's receipt carried, so no seat is ever confirmed to two different students.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: No student is left carrying a receipt forever — every receipt a student is issued is eventually consumed, either by confirming the seat or by being torn up once it no longer matches.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od9m9p5t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Centres, FeederCount, MaxEpoch, NOPERMIT

\* Feeders are numbered, and a feeder's number is its megawatt loading, so
\* the loadings are distinct and relief is not just a headcount.
Feeders == 1..FeederCount
Load(f) == f

\* dropped: feeders already tripped; relief: megawatts booked against the
\* shortfall; era: the reconfiguration epoch; permit: the outstanding permit
\* on each feeder, stamped with the epoch it was written under.
VARIABLES dropped, relief, era, permit

vars == <<dropped, relief, era, permit>>

TotalLoad == (FeederCount * (FeederCount + 1)) \div 2
Permits == [by: Centres, era: 0..MaxEpoch]

TypeOK ==
    /\ dropped \subseteq Feeders
    /\ relief \in 0..TotalLoad
    /\ era \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ permit \in [Feeders -> Permits \cup {NOPERMIT}]

Init ==
    /\ dropped = {}
    /\ relief = 0
    /\ era = 0
    /\ permit = [f \in Feeders |-> NOPERMIT]

SumLoad(S) ==
    LET Add[T \in SUBSET Feeders] ==
        IF T = {} THEN 0
        ELSE LET f == CHOOSE x \in T : TRUE IN Load(f) + Add[T \ {f}]
    IN Add[S]

Reconfigure ==
    /\ era < MaxEpoch
    /\ era' = era + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<dropped, relief, permit>>

Permit(c, f) ==
    /\ f \notin dropped
    /\ permit[f] = NOPERMIT
    /\ permit' = [permit EXCEPT ![f] = [by |-> c, era |-> era]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<dropped, relief, era>>

\* A trip needs this centre's own permit, at the epoch it was written under.
Trip(c, f) ==
    /\ f \notin dropped
    /\ permit[f] # NOPERMIT
    /\ permit[f].by = c
    /\ permit[f].era = era
    /\ dropped' = dropped \cup {f}
    /\ relief' = relief + Load(f)
    /\ permit' = [permit EXCEPT ![f] = NOPERMIT]
    /\ UNCHANGED era

Void(f) ==
    /\ permit[f] # NOPERMIT
    /\ permit[f].era # era
    /\ permit' = [permit EXCEPT ![f] = NOPERMIT]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<dropped, relief, era>>

Cancel(c, f) ==
    /\ permit[f] # NOPERMIT
    /\ permit[f].by = c /\ permit[f].era = era
    /\ permit' = [permit EXCEPT ![f] = NOPERMIT]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<dropped, relief, era>>

\* Everything is shed and no reconfiguration is left: the centres just wait.
Hold ==
    /\ dropped = Feeders
    /\ era = MaxEpoch
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ Reconfigure \/ Hold
    \/ \E f \in Feeders : Void(f)
    \/ \E c \in Centres, f \in Feeders : Permit(c, f) \/ Trip(c, f) \/ Cancel(c, f)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

ReliefMatchesWhatWasDropped == relief = SumLoad(dropped)
====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Centres = {primary, backup}
    FeederCount = 3
    MaxEpoch = 2
    NOPERMIT = NOPERMIT

INVARIANT ReliefMatchesWhatWasDropped
nl:
A regional power grid is protected by an automatic load shedder. Two control centres, a primary and a backup, run independently of each other but act on one shared pool of distribution feeders. Tripping a feeder is irreversible within the event: once a feeder is dropped it stays dropped for the duration, and the megawatts it was carrying are booked as relief against the shortfall the operators are trying to close.

Because both centres can see the same shortfall and reach for the same feeder, no centre trips anything on its own initiative. A centre must first take out a shed permit on a specific feeder, and a feeder carries at most one outstanding permit. Permits are stamped with the reconfiguration epoch that was current when they were taken out. The grid's topology is reconfigured under an epoch number — reclosers open, ties are thrown, and the feeder-to-substation map changes — and every reconfiguration advances the epoch, which makes every permit written under the old epoch worthless because the load behind that feeder is no longer what the permit was sized against.

A centre trips a feeder only by presenting its own permit at the epoch that permit names, and only for a feeder that is not already dropped; the trip consumes the permit and books that feeder's megawatts as relief. A stale permit is voided rather than honoured, and a centre may also simply cancel a permit it took out but decided not to use. Each feeder carries a known, distinct megawatt loading.

The full set of actions is: Reconfigure, in which the grid advances to the next reconfiguration epoch; Permit, in which a centre takes out a shed permit, stamped with the current epoch, on a feeder that is neither dropped nor already permitted; Trip, in which a centre presents its own current-epoch permit for a feeder that is not yet dropped, drops it, books its megawatts as relief, and consumes the permit; Void, in which a permit stamped with a superseded epoch is torn up; Cancel, in which the centre that took out a current-epoch permit gives it back unused; and Hold, in which the centres simply wait once every feeder has been dropped and no further reconfiguration is scheduled.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The total megawatts booked as relief is always exactly the sum of the loadings of the feeders that have been dropped, so no feeder's load is ever counted twice and no feeder is tripped more than once.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od8m6p6t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Frontends, MaxFence, PoolSize, NOBODY

\* holder: which front end currently holds the enrollment lease.
\* counter: the strictly increasing source of fencing numbers.
\* carried: the fencing number each front end still believes in (0 = none).
\* admitted: the fencing numbers the seat pool has accepted, in order.
VARIABLES holder, counter, carried, admitted, seats

vars == <<holder, counter, carried, admitted, seats>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ holder \in Frontends \cup {NOBODY}
    /\ counter \in 0..MaxFence
    /\ carried \in [Frontends -> 0..MaxFence]
    /\ admitted \in Seq(1..MaxFence)
    /\ seats \in 0..PoolSize

Init ==
    /\ holder = NOBODY
    /\ counter = 0
    /\ carried = [f \in Frontends |-> 0]
    /\ admitted = <<>>
    /\ seats = PoolSize

LastAdmitted == IF admitted = <<>> THEN 0 ELSE admitted[Len(admitted)]

Grant(f) ==
    /\ holder = NOBODY
    /\ counter < MaxFence
    /\ carried[f] = 0
    /\ holder' = f
    /\ counter' = counter + 1
    /\ carried' = [carried EXCEPT ![f] = counter + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<admitted, seats>>

\* The lease lapses silently; its holder is not told and keeps its number.
Lapse ==
    /\ holder # NOBODY
    /\ holder' = NOBODY
    /\ UNCHANGED <<counter, carried, admitted, seats>>

\* The pool, not the front end, is what rejects a stale actor.
Draw(f) ==
    /\ carried[f] # 0
    /\ seats > 0
    /\ carried[f] > LastAdmitted
    /\ admitted' = Append(admitted, carried[f])
    /\ carried' = [carried EXCEPT ![f] = 0]
    /\ seats' = seats - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, counter>>

Renounce(f) ==
    /\ carried[f] # 0
    /\ holder # f
    /\ carried' = [carried EXCEPT ![f] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, counter, admitted, seats>>

Restock ==
    /\ seats < PoolSize
    /\ seats' = seats + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, counter, carried, admitted>>

\* The counter is spent and nothing is outstanding: the add period is closed.
Close ==
    /\ counter = MaxFence
    /\ holder = NOBODY
    /\ \A f \in Frontends : carried[f] = 0
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

DrawStep == \E f \in Frontends : Draw(f)
RenounceStep == \E f \in Frontends : Renounce(f)

Next ==
    \/ \E f \in Frontends : Grant(f)
    \/ Lapse \/ DrawStep \/ RenounceStep \/ Restock \/ Close

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ WF_vars(Lapse) /\ WF_vars(DrawStep) /\ WF_vars(RenounceStep)

AdmittedFencesIncrease ==
    \A i \in 1..(Len(admitted) - 1) : admitted[i] < admitted[i + 1]

NoFenceIsCarriedForever ==
    \A f \in Frontends : (carried[f] # 0) ~> (carried[f] = 0)
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Frontends = {selfService, advisorOverride}
    MaxFence = 3
    PoolSize = 2
    NOBODY = NOBODY

INVARIANT AdmittedFencesIncrease

PROPERTY NoFenceIsCarriedForever
nl:
A university runs two independent registration front ends against one shared seat pool for a capstone course: the student self-service portal and the advising office's override portal. Neither knows what the other is doing. Both write into the same pool, so the registrar interposes a single enrollment lease: only the front end currently holding the lease is allowed to draw a seat.

The lease is time-bounded and lapses on its own. That is the awkward part, because a front end whose lease has lapsed does not find out at the moment it lapses — it goes on believing it is authorised until something tells it otherwise. To make that belief harmless the registrar hands out a fencing number with every lease: fencing numbers are drawn from a single strictly increasing counter, and the front end keeps the number it was given. The seat pool itself does the checking. It records the fencing number of every draw it accepts, and it refuses any draw whose number is not higher than the last number it accepted. A front end acting on a lapsed lease is therefore carrying an old number, and the pool turns it away rather than trusting it.

A front end uses its fencing number for a single draw: taking a seat consumes both the seat and the number. A front end that notices the lease is no longer held by it gives up its number without drawing. Seats also come back into the shared pool when students elsewhere drop the course, up to the pool's size.

The full set of actions is: Grant, in which the registrar gives the lease to a front end while no lease is outstanding, draws the next fencing number from the counter, and hands it over; Lapse, in which an outstanding lease quietly expires without telling its holder; Draw, in which a front end presents its fencing number to the seat pool, which accepts it only if it is higher than the last number the pool accepted, taking one seat and consuming the number; Renounce, in which a front end that no longer holds the lease gives up the number it was carrying; Restock, in which a dropped seat returns to the shared pool; and Close, in which the registrar simply waits once the fencing counter is spent, no lease is outstanding, and no front end is carrying a number.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The fencing numbers the seat pool has accepted, read in the order it accepted them, are strictly increasing, so no draw made on a lapsed lease is ever admitted after a newer one has already landed.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: No front end is left holding a fencing number forever — every number handed out is eventually either spent on a draw or given up.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od5m8p6t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Clients, Regions, LobbiesPer, RosterLimit, MaxForm, FREE, NOTICKET

Lobbies == [reg: Regions, idx: 1..LobbiesPer]

\* regionLock / lobbyLock: the coarse and fine levels of the scheme.
\* form: each lobby's formation number; ticket: what a client is carrying.
\* roster: seated entries, each stamped with the formation it was seated at.
VARIABLES regionLock, lobbyLock, form, ticket, roster

vars == <<regionLock, lobbyLock, form, ticket, roster>>

Tickets == [lobby: Lobbies, form: 0..MaxForm]
Entries == [who: Clients, form: 0..MaxForm]

TypeOK ==
    /\ regionLock \in [Regions -> Clients \cup {FREE}]
    /\ lobbyLock \in [Lobbies -> Clients \cup {FREE}]
    /\ form \in [Lobbies -> 0..MaxForm]
    /\ ticket \in [Clients -> Tickets \cup {NOTICKET}]
    /\ roster \in [Lobbies -> SUBSET Entries]

Init ==
    /\ regionLock = [r \in Regions |-> FREE]
    /\ lobbyLock = [l \in Lobbies |-> FREE]
    /\ form = [l \in Lobbies |-> 0]
    /\ ticket = [c \in Clients |-> NOTICKET]
    /\ roster = [l \in Lobbies |-> {}]

TakeRegion(c, r) ==
    /\ regionLock[r] = FREE
    /\ ticket[c] = NOTICKET
    /\ regionLock' = [regionLock EXCEPT ![r] = c]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lobbyLock, form, ticket, roster>>

\* The fine lock is taken under the coarse one, which is dropped at once.
TakeLobby(c, l) ==
    /\ regionLock[l.reg] = c
    /\ lobbyLock[l] = FREE
    /\ ticket[c] = NOTICKET
    /\ lobbyLock' = [lobbyLock EXCEPT ![l] = c]
    /\ regionLock' = [regionLock EXCEPT ![l.reg] = FREE]
    /\ ticket' = [ticket EXCEPT ![c] = [lobby |-> l, form |-> form[l]]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<form, roster>>

Seat(c) ==
    /\ ticket[c] # NOTICKET
    /\ LET tk == ticket[c] IN
        /\ form[tk.lobby] = tk.form
        /\ Cardinality(roster[tk.lobby]) < RosterLimit
        /\ roster' = [roster EXCEPT ![tk.lobby] =
                        @ \cup {[who |-> c, form |-> tk.form]}]
        /\ lobbyLock' = [lobbyLock EXCEPT ![tk.lobby] = FREE]
    /\ ticket' = [ticket EXCEPT ![c] = NOTICKET]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<regionLock, form>>

Scrap(c) ==
    /\ ticket[c] # NOTICKET
    /\ form[ticket[c].lobby] # ticket[c].form
    /\ lobbyLock' = [lobbyLock EXCEPT ![ticket[c].lobby] = FREE]
    /\ ticket' = [ticket EXCEPT ![c] = NOTICKET]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<regionLock, form, roster>>

\* Re-forming does not wait for whoever is sitting on the lobby's lock.
Reform(l) ==
    /\ form[l] < MaxForm
    /\ form' = [form EXCEPT ![l] = @ + 1]
    /\ roster' = [roster EXCEPT ![l] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<regionLock, lobbyLock, ticket>>

Leave(l, e) ==
    /\ e \in roster[l]
    /\ roster' = [roster EXCEPT ![l] = @ \ {e}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<regionLock, lobbyLock, form, ticket>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Clients, r \in Regions : TakeRegion(c, r)
    \/ \E c \in Clients, l \in Lobbies : TakeLobby(c, l)
    \/ \E c \in Clients : Seat(c) \/ Scrap(c)
    \/ \E l \in Lobbies : Reform(l) \/ (\E e \in roster[l] : Leave(l, e))

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

RosterMatchesCurrentFormation ==
    \A l \in Lobbies : \A e \in roster[l] : e.form = form[l]
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Clients = {c1, c2}
    Regions = {eu, na}
    LobbiesPer = 1
    RosterLimit = 2
    MaxForm = 2
    FREE = FREE
    NOTICKET = NOTICKET

INVARIANT RosterMatchesCurrentFormation
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker builds match rosters. Lobbies are grouped by region, and a client that wants a place is put through a two-level scheme: it must first take the region's coarse lock, and only while holding that may it take the lock on one lobby inside the region. Taking the lobby lock releases the region lock and hands the client a seating ticket recording the lobby and that lobby's formation number as it stood at that instant.

Formation numbers matter because the matchmaker re-forms lobbies on its own schedule. Re-forming a lobby tears down its roster completely and advances its formation number, and it does this whether or not a client is sitting on that lobby's lock — the matchmaker will not let one client stall a whole region's matchmaking.

Clients can be slow but they do not fail. A slow client keeps its ticket and eventually gets around to seating itself, possibly long after the lobby it was looking at has been re-formed. That is why the seating step re-checks the ticket: a client is seated only if the ticket's formation number still equals the lobby's current formation number, and the roster entry it creates records the formation number the ticket carried. A client whose ticket names a superseded formation throws the ticket away and releases the lobby lock without being seated. A seated client can leave its roster.

The full set of actions is: TakeRegion, in which a client takes a free region lock; TakeLobby, in which a client holding a region lock takes a free lobby lock inside that region, releases the region lock, and receives a ticket carrying the lobby's current formation number; Seat, in which a client whose ticket still matches its lobby's formation number is added to that lobby's roster below the roster limit, consuming the ticket and releasing the lobby lock; Scrap, in which a client whose ticket names a superseded formation discards it and releases the lobby lock; Reform, in which the matchmaker clears a lobby's roster and advances its formation number regardless of who holds its lock; and Leave, in which a seated client is removed from a roster.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every entry on a lobby's roster carries that lobby's current formation number, so nobody sits on a roster on the strength of a ticket that a re-formation has already superseded.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od16m1p5t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS CounterCount, ScriptsPer, ShelfCapacity

Counters == 1..CounterCount
\* A prescription is taken in by one counter, and only that counter fills it.
Scripts == [at: Counters, no: 1..ScriptsPer]

\* token: which counter currently holds the ring's dispensing token.
\* register: the permanent record of what has been handed out.
\* eligible: prescriptions the pharmacist has verified; vault: shared stock.
VARIABLES token, register, eligible, vault

vars == <<token, register, eligible, vault>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ token \in Counters
    /\ register \in Seq(Scripts)
    /\ eligible \subseteq Scripts
    /\ vault \in 0..ShelfCapacity

Init ==
    /\ token = 1
    /\ register = <<>>
    /\ eligible = {}
    /\ vault = 0

InRegister(s) == \E i \in 1..Len(register) : register[i] = s

Verify(s) ==
    /\ s \notin eligible
    /\ ~InRegister(s)
    /\ eligible' = eligible \cup {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, register, vault>>

\* The token moves one place around the ring and wraps at the end.
Pass ==
    /\ token' = (token % CounterCount) + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<register, eligible, vault>>

Fill(s) ==
    /\ s \in eligible
    /\ s.at = token
    /\ ~InRegister(s)
    /\ vault > 0
    /\ register' = Append(register, s)
    /\ eligible' = eligible \ {s}
    /\ vault' = vault - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED token

Restock ==
    /\ vault < ShelfCapacity
    /\ vault' = vault + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, register, eligible>>

VerifyStep == \E s \in Scripts : Verify(s)
FillStep == \E s \in Scripts : Fill(s)

Next == VerifyStep \/ Pass \/ FillStep \/ Restock

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ WF_vars(VerifyStep) /\ WF_vars(Pass) /\ WF_vars(Restock)
        /\ SF_vars(FillStep)

RegisterHasNoDuplicate ==
    \A i, j \in 1..Len(register) : register[i] = register[j] => i = j
