SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    CounterCount = 2
    ScriptsPer = 2
    ShelfCapacity = 2

INVARIANT RegisterHasNoDuplicate

PROPERTY SomethingIsEventuallyDispensed
nl:
A hospital pharmacy runs two dispensing counters that operate independently but draw controlled-substance packs from one shared vault stock. Handing a pack across the counter is irreversible: once a prescription has been dispensed it cannot be un-dispensed, and dispensing the same prescription twice would put a second controlled pack into circulation against a single authorisation.

Exclusive access to the vault is arranged with a token ring. The counters are wired in a ring and exactly one dispensing token circulates around it. A counter may only take stock from the vault while it is holding the token, and the token moves on to the next counter in the ring when the holder is done with it. Each prescription belongs to the counter that took it in, so a prescription is only ever dispensed by its own counter, and only while that counter holds the token.

A prescription becomes eligible for dispensing when the pharmacist verifies it against the patient record. Filling a verified prescription takes one pack out of the shared vault stock and writes the prescription into the dispensing register, which is the pharmacy's permanent record of what has been handed out; a prescription already written into that register is never filled again. The vault is restocked from the wholesaler up to its shelf capacity.

The full set of actions is: Verify, in which a pharmacist checks a prescription against the patient record and marks it eligible for dispensing; Pass, in which the counter holding the dispensing token hands it to the next counter around the ring; Fill, in which the counter holding the token dispenses one of its own eligible prescriptions that is not already in the register, taking a pack from the shared vault stock and writing the prescription into the register; and Restock, in which the wholesaler adds a pack to the vault, up to shelf capacity.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No prescription appears more than once in the dispensing register, so no authorisation is ever dispensed against twice.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Some prescription eventually reaches the dispensing register, because the token keeps circulating and the vault keeps being restocked, so an eligible prescription's own counter eventually gets both the token and the stock it needs.

---- MODULE W4Od11m9p3t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Jobs, SlotCount, MaxEpoch, JournalLimit, NONE, DONE

Slots == 1..SlotCount

\* lineup: the reconfiguration number now in force.
\* table: the slot occupancy of the running lineup, wiped on reconfiguration.
\* journal: permanent, never rewritten, spanning superseded lineups.
\* booking: each job's outstanding reservation, stamped when it was filed.
VARIABLES lineup, table, journal, booking

vars == <<lineup, table, journal, booking>>

Entries == [job: Jobs, slot: Slots, lineup: 0..MaxEpoch]
Bookings == [slot: Slots, lineup: 0..MaxEpoch]

TypeOK ==
    /\ lineup \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ table \in [Slots -> Jobs \cup {NONE, DONE}]
    /\ journal \in Seq(Entries)
    /\ booking \in [Jobs -> Bookings \cup {NONE}]

Init ==
    /\ lineup = 0
    /\ table = [s \in Slots |-> NONE]
    /\ journal = <<>>
    /\ booking = [j \in Jobs |-> NONE]

Scheduled(j) == \E s \in Slots : table[s] = j

File(j, s) ==
    /\ booking[j] = NONE
    /\ ~Scheduled(j)
    /\ booking' = [booking EXCEPT ![j] = [slot |-> s, lineup |-> lineup]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lineup, table, journal>>

\* The stamp must still be current and the slot still free in this lineup.
Commit(j) ==
    /\ booking[j] # NONE
    /\ Len(journal) < JournalLimit
    /\ booking[j].lineup = lineup
    /\ table[booking[j].slot] = NONE
    /\ table' = [table EXCEPT ![booking[j].slot] = j]
    /\ journal' = Append(journal, [job |-> j, slot |-> booking[j].slot,
                                   lineup |-> lineup])
    /\ booking' = [booking EXCEPT ![j] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED lineup

Toss(j) ==
    /\ booking[j] # NONE
    /\ \/ booking[j].lineup # lineup
       \/ table[booking[j].slot] # NONE
    /\ booking' = [booking EXCEPT ![j] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lineup, table, journal>>

\* A finished job leaves its slot marked spent; the slot only reopens at the
\* next reconfiguration, so this lineup cannot hand it out a second time.
Unspool(j, s) ==
    /\ table[s] = j
    /\ table' = [table EXCEPT ![s] = DONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lineup, journal, booking>>

Reconfigure ==
    /\ lineup < MaxEpoch
    /\ lineup' = lineup + 1
    /\ table' = [s \in Slots |-> NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<journal, booking>>

\* The override skips the queue, never the physical occupancy of the slot.
Override(j, s) ==
    /\ Len(journal) < JournalLimit
    /\ table[s] = NONE
    /\ ~Scheduled(j)
    /\ table' = [table EXCEPT ![s] = j]
    /\ journal' = Append(journal, [job |-> j, slot |-> s, lineup |-> lineup])
    /\ booking' = [booking EXCEPT ![j] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED lineup

\* The shift's journal is full and the lineup is final: the spooler stands down.
ShiftOver ==
    /\ Len(journal) = JournalLimit
    /\ lineup = MaxEpoch
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E j \in Jobs, s \in Slots : File(j, s) \/ Override(j, s) \/ Unspool(j, s)
    \/ \E j \in Jobs : Commit(j) \/ Toss(j)
    \/ Reconfigure \/ ShiftOver

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CurrentLineupSlotsAreUnique ==
    \A i, k \in 1..Len(journal) :

         /\ journal[k].lineup = lineup
         /\ journal[i].slot = journal[k].slot) => i = k

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Jobs = {jobA, jobB}
    SlotCount = 2
    MaxEpoch = 1
    JournalLimit = 3
    NONE = NONE
    DONE = DONE

INVARIANT CurrentLineupSlotsAreUnique
nl:
A commercial print shop spools jobs onto press time slots. The shop's press lineup is not stable through the day: presses are swapped, a folder goes down, a rush contract takes a line out. Every such change is a reconfiguration, and reconfigurations are numbered. Advancing the reconfiguration number wipes the current slot table clean — all slots reopen, because the slots of the old lineup do not mean the same thing as the slots of the new one.

The spooler keeps a permanent assignment journal. Every time a job is put into a slot, an entry is written recording the job, the slot, and the reconfiguration number in force at that moment. The journal is never rewritten, so it accumulates entries from superseded lineups alongside entries from the current one. A slot vacated by a finished job is marked spent rather than free, so it is not handed out again until the next reconfiguration. Slots may legitimately be reused across reconfigurations; what must never happen is two jobs landing in the same slot of the same lineup.

An operator books a slot in two steps: it first files a reservation naming the slot and stamped with the reconfiguration number it saw, and the spooler later commits that reservation. The commit goes through only if the reservation's number still matches the current reconfiguration and the slot is still free in the current slot table. A reservation that fails either test is thrown out and the operator files a fresh one. The journal has a fixed length for the shift and no entries are written once it is full.

The shop manager has a privileged override. The manager can push a job straight into a slot without filing a reservation and without waiting for the queue — that is the whole point of the override. What the override does not skip is the slot table: the manager cannot push a job into a slot that is already occupied in the current lineup, because the press physically cannot run two jobs at once. An override consumes any reservation the job had outstanding.

The full set of actions is: File, in which an unscheduled job's operator files a reservation for a slot, stamped with the current reconfiguration number; Commit, in which a reservation whose stamp still matches and whose slot is still free is written into the slot table and appended to the journal; Toss, in which a reservation whose stamp is stale or whose slot has been taken is discarded; Reconfigure, in which the press lineup changes, advancing the reconfiguration number and clearing the slot table; Override, in which the manager pushes a job directly into a free slot of the current lineup, appending to the journal and consuming any reservation that job had outstanding; Unspool, in which a job that has finished printing comes off its slot, leaving that slot marked spent for the rest of the lineup rather than free; and ShiftOver, in which the spooler simply stands down once the journal is full and no further reconfiguration is scheduled.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Among the journal entries written under the current reconfiguration number, no slot appears more than once, so no press slot of the running lineup is ever allocated to two jobs.

---- MODULE W4Od18m7p2t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Locks, SlotCount, Budget, MaxTune, EMPTY

Slots == 1..SlotCount

\* reserve: credits still at the hub; allowance: credits at each lock.
\* counter: the lock's compare-and-swap value; slot: grant slots, delivered
\* to the locks in whatever order the mesh happens to manage.
VARIABLES reserve, allowance, counter, slot

vars == <<reserve, allowance, counter, slot>>

Grants == [to: Locks, amt: 1..Budget, seen: 0..MaxTune]

TypeOK ==
    /\ reserve \in 0..Budget
    /\ allowance \in [Locks -> 0..Budget]
    /\ counter \in [Locks -> 0..MaxTune]
    /\ slot \in [Slots -> Grants \cup {EMPTY}]

Init ==
    /\ reserve = Budget
    /\ allowance = [l \in Locks |-> 0]
    /\ counter = [l \in Locks |-> 0]
    /\ slot = [i \in Slots |-> EMPTY]

Held == LET f[S \in SUBSET Locks] ==
            IF S = {} THEN 0
            ELSE LET l == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN allowance[l] + f[S \ {l}]
        IN f[Locks]

InFlight == LET g[S \in SUBSET Slots] ==
                IF S = {} THEN 0
                ELSE LET i == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE
                     IN (IF slot[i] = EMPTY THEN 0 ELSE slot[i].amt) + g[S \ {i}]
            IN g[Slots]

\* The reserve is debited the instant the grant is handed to the radio.
Issue(l, n, i) ==
    /\ slot[i] = EMPTY
    /\ n <= reserve
    /\ reserve' = reserve - n
    /\ slot' = [slot EXCEPT ![i] = [to |-> l, amt |-> n, seen |-> counter[l]]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<allowance, counter>>

Apply(i) ==
    /\ slot[i] # EMPTY
    /\ counter[slot[i].to] = slot[i].seen
    /\ allowance' = [allowance EXCEPT ![slot[i].to] = @ + slot[i].amt]
    /\ counter' = [counter EXCEPT ![slot[i].to] = @ + 1]
    /\ slot' = [slot EXCEPT ![i] = EMPTY]
    /\ UNCHANGED reserve

\* A grant the lock will not honour goes back whole, never partly.
Bounce(i) ==
    /\ slot[i] # EMPTY
    /\ counter[slot[i].to] # slot[i].seen
    /\ reserve' = reserve + slot[i].amt
    /\ slot' = [slot EXCEPT ![i] = EMPTY]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<allowance, counter>>

Return(l, n) ==
    /\ n <= allowance[l]
    /\ allowance' = [allowance EXCEPT ![l] = @ - n]
    /\ reserve' = reserve + n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<counter, slot>>

Retune(l) ==
    /\ counter[l] < MaxTune
    /\ counter' = [counter EXCEPT ![l] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reserve, allowance, slot>>

Next ==
    \/ \E l \in Locks, n \in 1..Budget, i \in Slots : Issue(l, n, i)
    \/ \E i \in Slots : Apply(i) \/ Bounce(i)
    \/ \E l \in Locks, n \in 1..Budget : Return(l, n)
    \/ \E l \in Locks : Retune(l)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CreditsAreConserved == reserve + Held + InFlight = Budget

\* Counters advance on every applied grant, so the run is cut off once every
\* lock has been re-stamped MaxTune times.
CounterBound == \A l \in Locks : counter[l] <= MaxTune
====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Locks = {frontDoor, sideDoor}
    SlotCount = 2
    Budget = 2
    MaxTune = 3
    EMPTY = EMPTY

INVARIANT CreditsAreConserved

CONSTRAINT CounterBound
nl:
A smart-home door lock network runs on a fixed budget of radio airtime credits. The house hub owns the budget: credits sit either in the hub's own reserve, or in a lock's local allowance, or in a grant that is on its way from the hub to a lock. Credits are never minted and never destroyed — the installer sizes the budget once, and every credit in the house is always in exactly one of those three places.

Grants travel over the same mesh radio the locks use for everything else, and that mesh does not preserve order. A grant handed to the mesh may be delivered before or after grants handed over later, and the hub has a small fixed number of outgoing grant slots; it can only issue a grant when a slot is free. The hub debits its reserve at the moment it issues the grant, not when the grant lands, because the credits are committed the instant they are handed to the radio.

Each lock exposes a compare-and-swap counter that changes whenever its allowance changes and whenever its radio profile is re-tuned. A grant records the value of that counter as the hub read it. A lock applies a grant only if its counter still equals the value the grant recorded; applying adds the credits to the lock's allowance and advances the counter. If the counter has moved on, the grant describes an allowance the lock no longer has, so it is bounced: the grant is dropped and its credits go straight back to the hub's reserve, never to a lock. Locks also hand credits back to the hub directly when they are running quiet, which needs no grant.

The full set of actions is: Issue, in which the hub debits its reserve and puts a grant naming a lock, an amount, and that lock's current counter value into a free grant slot; Apply, in which a lock whose counter still matches a waiting grant takes its credits into its allowance, advances its counter, and frees the slot; Bounce, in which a grant whose recorded counter no longer matches its lock is dropped, its credits returned to the hub's reserve, and its slot freed; Return, in which a lock hands some of its allowance back to the hub directly; and Retune, in which a lock's radio profile changes, advancing its counter and so invalidating any grant already in flight to it.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The credits in the hub's reserve, plus the allowances held across all the locks, plus the credits sitting in grants that are still in flight, always add up to exactly the fixed budget the installer configured.

---- MODULE W4Od12m6p3t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Hospitals, Units, LeaseFull, RefreshCap, FREE, NOUNIT

\* shelf: the bank's record of who a unit is reserved to.
\* worklist: the hospital's own record of what it is holding.
\* countdown: the lease timer; refreshes: how many refreshes are left.
VARIABLES shelf, worklist, countdown, refreshes, up

vars == <<shelf, worklist, countdown, refreshes, up>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ shelf \in [Units -> Hospitals \cup {FREE}]
    /\ worklist \in [Hospitals -> Units \cup {NOUNIT}]
    /\ countdown \in [Units -> 0..LeaseFull]
    /\ refreshes \in [Units -> 0..RefreshCap]
    /\ up \in [Hospitals -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
    /\ shelf = [u \in Units |-> FREE]
    /\ worklist = [h \in Hospitals |-> NOUNIT]
    /\ countdown = [u \in Units |-> 0]
    /\ refreshes = [u \in Units |-> RefreshCap]
    /\ up = [h \in Hospitals |-> TRUE]

\* Both records are written in the same step, always.
Reserve(h, u) ==
    /\ up[h]
    /\ shelf[u] = FREE /\ worklist[h] = NOUNIT
    /\ shelf' = [shelf EXCEPT ![u] = h]
    /\ worklist' = [worklist EXCEPT ![h] = u]
    /\ countdown' = [countdown EXCEPT ![u] = LeaseFull]
    /\ refreshes' = [refreshes EXCEPT ![u] = RefreshCap]
    /\ UNCHANGED up

Refresh(h, u) ==
    /\ up[h]
    /\ shelf[u] = h
    /\ refreshes[u] > 0
    /\ countdown' = [countdown EXCEPT ![u] = LeaseFull]
    /\ refreshes' = [refreshes EXCEPT ![u] = @ - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, worklist, up>>

Tick(u) ==
    /\ shelf[u] # FREE
    /\ countdown[u] > 0
    /\ countdown' = [countdown EXCEPT ![u] = @ - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, worklist, refreshes, up>>

\* The bank lapses on its own authority; a silent hospital is not consulted.
Lapse(u) ==
    /\ shelf[u] # FREE
    /\ countdown[u] = 0
    /\ worklist' = [worklist EXCEPT ![shelf[u]] = NOUNIT]
    /\ shelf' = [shelf EXCEPT ![u] = FREE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<countdown, refreshes, up>>

Release(h, u) ==
    /\ up[h]
    /\ shelf[u] = h /\ worklist[h] = u
    /\ shelf' = [shelf EXCEPT ![u] = FREE]
    /\ worklist' = [worklist EXCEPT ![h] = NOUNIT]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<countdown, refreshes, up>>

Silence(h) ==
    /\ \A g \in Hospitals : up[g]
    /\ up' = [up EXCEPT ![h] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, worklist, countdown, refreshes>>

Rejoin(h) ==
    /\ ~up[h]
    /\ up' = [up EXCEPT ![h] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, worklist, countdown, refreshes>>

TickStep == \E u \in Units : Tick(u)
LapseStep == \E u \in Units : Lapse(u)
Fairness == \A u \in Units : WF_vars(Tick(u)) /\ WF_vars(Lapse(u))

Next ==
    \/ \E h \in Hospitals, u \in Units : Reserve(h, u) \/ Refresh(h, u)
                                          \/ Release(h, u)
    \/ TickStep \/ LapseStep
    \/ \E h \in Hospitals : Silence(h) \/ Rejoin(h)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ Fairness

RecordsAgreeBothWays ==
    \A u \in Units, h \in Hospitals :
        (shelf[u] = h) <=> (worklist[h] = u)

NoUnitStaysReserved ==
    \A u \in Units : (shelf[u] # FREE) ~> (shelf[u] = FREE)
====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Hospitals = {stMarys, cityGeneral}
    Units = {bagA, bagB}
    LeaseFull = 2
    RefreshCap = 1
    FREE = FREE
    NOUNIT = NOUNIT

INVARIANT RecordsAgreeBothWays

PROPERTY NoUnitStaysReserved
nl:
A regional blood bank tracks individual units of blood and reserves them for hospitals that are preparing to transfuse. A unit is a physical bag on a shelf, so a reservation is an exclusive claim on that specific bag: two hospitals cannot both be told they have it.

The bank does not hand out permanent reservations, because a hospital can go silent at any moment — its interface drops, its theatre list changes, the requesting clinician goes off shift — and a bag held for a hospital that has stopped talking is a bag that will time-expire on the shelf. So every reservation is a lease with a countdown. The countdown ticks down as time passes, and a hospital that is still up and still wants the bag can refresh it back to full. Refreshing is not unlimited: a reservation may only be refreshed a fixed number of times before the bank insists on letting it lapse, so that a hospital cannot pin a scarce unit indefinitely.

The reservation is recorded twice, once on each side of the arrangement: the bank's shelf record says which hospital a unit is reserved to, and the hospital's own worklist says which unit it is holding. Every action that changes a reservation changes both records in the same step — placing one, letting one lapse, or releasing one — because a shelf record and a worklist that disagree is exactly how the same bag ends up promised to two hospitals.

When the countdown reaches zero the bank lapses the reservation on its own authority, without asking the hospital, which is what makes silent failure survivable. A hospital that is up can also release a unit it holds, returning it to the shelf. At most one hospital is out at a time, and one that went silent can come back.

The full set of actions is: Reserve, in which a hospital that is up and holding nothing takes an unreserved unit, recording it on both sides and starting the countdown at full with its refresh allowance reset; Refresh, in which a hospital that is up restores the countdown on a unit it holds, consuming one of its refresh allowance; Tick, in which a running countdown decreases by one; Lapse, in which the bank clears a reservation whose countdown has reached zero, clearing both records; Release, in which a hospital that is up gives a unit it holds back to the shelf, clearing both records; Silence, in which a hospital that is up stops responding while every other hospital is still up; and Rejoin, in which the silent hospital comes back.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every unit and every hospital, the bank's shelf record shows that unit reserved to that hospital exactly when the hospital's worklist shows it holding that unit, so a unit is never promised to two hospitals at once.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: No unit stays reserved forever — every reservation the bank places is eventually cleared, because the countdown runs down and the refresh allowance is finite.

---- MODULE W4Od11m5p2t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Supervisors, Spoolers, Stock, Quorum

\* shelf: reams available in the store room.
\* cutPile: reams already cut against a spooler's pending draw.
\* press: reams loaded into each spooler; endorsed: who has endorsed a draw.
VARIABLES shelf, cutPile, press, endorsed

vars == <<shelf, cutPile, press, endorsed>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ shelf \in 0..Stock
    /\ cutPile \in [Spoolers -> 0..Stock]
    /\ press \in [Spoolers -> 0..Stock]
    /\ endorsed \in [Spoolers -> SUBSET Supervisors]

Init ==
    /\ shelf = Stock
    /\ cutPile = [s \in Spoolers |-> 0]
    /\ press = [s \in Spoolers |-> 0]
    /\ endorsed = [s \in Spoolers |-> {}]

Total(f) == LET add[S \in SUBSET Spoolers] ==
                IF S = {} THEN 0
                ELSE LET s == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN f[s] + add[S \ {s}]
            IN add[Spoolers]

\* Cutting takes the reams off the shelf at once: cut paper is not available.
SetAside(sp, n) ==
    /\ cutPile[sp] = 0
    /\ endorsed[sp] = {}
    /\ n <= shelf
    /\ shelf' = shelf - n
    /\ cutPile' = [cutPile EXCEPT ![sp] = n]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<press, endorsed>>

Endorse(sp, v) ==
    /\ cutPile[sp] > 0
    /\ v \notin endorsed[sp]
    /\ endorsed' = [endorsed EXCEPT ![sp] = @ \cup {v}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, cutPile, press>>

Load(sp) ==
    /\ cutPile[sp] > 0
    /\ Cardinality(endorsed[sp]) >= Quorum
    /\ press' = [press EXCEPT ![sp] = @ + cutPile[sp]]
    /\ cutPile' = [cutPile EXCEPT ![sp] = 0]
    /\ endorsed' = [endorsed EXCEPT ![sp] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED shelf

Rescind(sp) ==
    /\ cutPile[sp] > 0
    /\ Cardinality(endorsed[sp]) < Quorum
    /\ shelf' = shelf + cutPile[sp]
    /\ cutPile' = [cutPile EXCEPT ![sp] = 0]
    /\ endorsed' = [endorsed EXCEPT ![sp] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED press

Return(sp, n) ==
    /\ n > 0
    /\ n <= press[sp]
    /\ press' = [press EXCEPT ![sp] = @ - n]
    /\ shelf' = shelf + n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cutPile, endorsed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E sp \in Spoolers, n \in 1..Stock : SetAside(sp, n) \/ Return(sp, n)
    \/ \E sp \in Spoolers, v \in Supervisors : Endorse(sp, v)
    \/ \E sp \in Spoolers : Load(sp) \/ Rescind(sp)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

PaperIsConserved == shelf + Total(cutPile) + Total(press) = Stock
====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Supervisors = {sup1, sup2, sup3}
    Spoolers = {sheetFed, web}
    Stock = 3
    Quorum = 2

INVARIANT PaperIsConserved
nl:
A print shop runs two spoolers — the sheet-fed spooler and the web spooler — that schedule jobs completely independently of one another. What ties them together is paper: both draw reams of the same house stock from a single store room, and the shop's stock control is only meaningful if reams are never conjured up and never quietly vanish. A ream is always in exactly one of three places: on the shelf in the store room, cut and set aside against one of the spoolers, or loaded into that spooler's press.

Neither spooler may take stock on its own say-so, because a spooler that grabs reams for a long run can starve the other one mid-shift. Instead each spooler's draw is put to the shift supervisors and needs a quorum of them to endorse it. The two spoolers can have draws in flight at the same time and are voted on separately — one spooler's pending draw does not block the other's.

A draw begins by setting reams aside: the reams come off the shelf immediately and sit in that spooler's cut pile, because paper that has been physically cut for a run cannot also be counted as available on the shelf. The supervisors then endorse one at a time. When a spooler's endorsements reach quorum, the draw is loaded: the cut pile goes into that spooler's press and the tally of endorsements is wiped ready for the next draw. A draw that has not reached quorum can instead be rescinded, in which case the cut pile goes back on the shelf whole and the endorsements are wiped. A spooler has at most one draw in flight at a time. Reams that a press did not end up needing are returned to the shelf directly, which needs no vote.

The full set of actions is: SetAside, in which a spooler with no draw in flight moves some reams off the shelf into its own cut pile; Endorse, in which one supervisor who has not yet endorsed a spooler's pending draw adds an endorsement; Load, in which a spooler whose pending draw has reached quorum moves its cut pile into its press and clears its endorsements; Rescind, in which a spooler's pending draw that has not reached quorum is abandoned, its cut pile returned to the shelf and its endorsements cleared; and Return, in which a spooler puts unused reams from its press back on the shelf.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The reams on the store-room shelf, plus the reams cut and set aside against each spooler, plus the reams loaded into each spooler's press, always add up to exactly the house stock the shop holds.

---- MODULE W4Od5m6p1t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Leaders, Slots, MinSize, MaxSize, NOBODY, NOSNAP, NORECEIPT

\* record: the shared claim list. lease: who may prepare or write.
\* snap: the captured read plus the slot to add. receipt: each leader's note
\* of the claim it last committed. size: the lobby size, tuned at runtime.
VARIABLES record, lease, snap, receipt, size

vars == <<record, lease, snap, receipt, size>>

Snaps == [saw: SUBSET Slots, add: Slots]

TypeOK ==
    /\ record \subseteq Slots
    /\ lease \in Leaders \cup {NOBODY}
    /\ snap \in [Leaders -> Snaps \cup {NOSNAP}]
    /\ receipt \in [Leaders -> Slots \cup {NORECEIPT}]
    /\ size \in MinSize..MaxSize

Init ==
    /\ record = {}
    /\ lease = NOBODY
    /\ snap = [l \in Leaders |-> NOSNAP]
    /\ receipt = [l \in Leaders |-> NORECEIPT]
    /\ size = MinSize

\* A leader still carrying a snapshot may not take a fresh lease.
Take(l) ==
    /\ lease = NOBODY
    /\ snap[l] = NOSNAP
    /\ lease' = l
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, snap, receipt, size>>

Prepare(l, s) ==
    /\ lease = l
    /\ snap[l] = NOSNAP
    /\ s \notin record
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![l] = [saw |-> record, add |-> s]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, lease, receipt, size>>

\* The write replaces the record wholesale with what this leader saw.
Write(l) ==
    /\ lease = l
    /\ snap[l] # NOSNAP
    /\ Cardinality(snap[l].saw \cup {snap[l].add}) <= size
    /\ record' = snap[l].saw \cup {snap[l].add}
    /\ receipt' = [receipt EXCEPT ![l] = snap[l].add]
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![l] = NOSNAP]
    /\ lease' = NOBODY
    /\ UNCHANGED size

Expire ==
    /\ lease # NOBODY
    /\ lease' = NOBODY
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, snap, receipt, size>>

Discard(l) ==
    /\ snap[l] # NOSNAP
    /\ lease # l
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![l] = NOSNAP]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, lease, receipt, size>>

Resize ==
    /\ \E n \in MinSize..MaxSize :
        /\ Cardinality(record) <= n
        /\ size' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, lease, snap, receipt>>

WriteStep == \E l \in Leaders : Write(l)
DiscardStep == \E l \in Leaders : Discard(l)

Next ==
    \/ \E l \in Leaders : Take(l)
    \/ \E l \in Leaders, s \in Slots : Prepare(l, s)
    \/ WriteStep \/ DiscardStep \/ Expire \/ Resize

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ WF_vars(Expire)
        /\ \A l \in Leaders : WF_vars(Discard(l)) /\ SF_vars(Write(l))

CommittedClaimsSurvive ==
    \A l \in Leaders : receipt[l] # NORECEIPT => receipt[l] \in record

NoSnapshotIsHeldForever ==
    \A l \in Leaders : (snap[l] # NOSNAP) ~> (snap[l] = NOSNAP)
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Leaders = {redLead, blueLead}
    Slots = {slotA, slotB}
    MinSize = 1
    MaxSize = 2
    NOBODY = NOBODY
    NOSNAP = NOSNAP
    NORECEIPT = NORECEIPT

INVARIANT CommittedClaimsSurvive

PROPERTY NoSnapshotIsHeldForever
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker keeps one shared lobby record listing which loadout slots have been claimed. Party leaders edit that record, and because the record is a single blob that clients read and write back whole, an edit is a read-modify-write: a leader reads the current claim list, adds the slot it wants, and writes the whole list back. That is exactly the shape in which one leader's edit can silently erase another's.

The matchmaker's defence is a write lease. Only the leader currently holding the lease may prepare an edit or write one back, and preparing an edit is what captures the snapshot the leader will write from. Leases expire on their own — a leader that goes quiet does not hold the record hostage — and a leader whose lease has gone must throw away the snapshot it captured rather than write from it, because that snapshot may already be behind. A leader with a snapshot in hand cannot take a fresh lease until it has thrown the stale one away, so a snapshot captured under one lease is never written back under another.

When a leader writes, the record becomes exactly the snapshot it captured plus the slot it claimed, and the leader keeps a note of the claim it just committed as its own receipt from the matchmaker. Writing also gives up the lease.

The lobby's size is tuned at runtime — the matchmaker grows or shrinks the lobby as queue depth and server capacity change — and a write is only accepted if the resulting claim list fits within the size then in force. The matchmaker never shrinks the lobby below the number of claims already in the record, because a claim already accepted cannot be revoked by a resize.

The full set of actions is: Take, in which a leader that holds no snapshot takes the free write lease; Prepare, in which the lease holder captures the current claim list as its snapshot and picks an unclaimed slot; Write, in which the lease holder replaces the record with its snapshot plus its chosen slot, provided the result fits the current lobby size, records its receipt, and gives up the lease; Expire, in which an outstanding lease lapses on its own; Discard, in which a leader that no longer holds the lease throws away the snapshot it captured; and Resize, in which the matchmaker sets the lobby size to any supported value that still covers every claim already in the record.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every claim a leader holds a receipt for is still present in the shared record, so no committed claim is ever erased by another leader writing back an older view of the record.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: No leader is left holding a captured snapshot forever — every snapshot is eventually either written back or thrown away.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od13m1p0t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS MachineCount, PerNetwork, BatchLimit, IDLE

Machines == 1..MachineCount
Networks == 1..(MachineCount \div PerNetwork)
NetOf(m) == ((m - 1) \div PerNetwork) + 1

\* token: the machine holding the ring's transmit token.
\* onModem: each network's record of which of its machines is keying.
\* queued: machines with readings waiting; uploaded: batches sent per network.
VARIABLES token, onModem, queued, uploaded

vars == <<token, onModem, queued, uploaded>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ token \in Machines
    /\ onModem \in [Networks -> Machines \cup {IDLE}]
    /\ queued \subseteq Machines
    /\ uploaded \in [Networks -> 0..BatchLimit]

Init ==
    /\ token = 1
    /\ onModem = [n \in Networks |-> IDLE]
    /\ queued = {}
    /\ uploaded = [n \in Networks |-> 0]

Queue(m) ==
    /\ m \notin queued
    /\ onModem[NetOf(m)] = IDLE
    /\ queued' = queued \cup {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, onModem, uploaded>>

Seize(m) ==
    /\ token = m
    /\ m \in queued
    /\ onModem[NetOf(m)] = IDLE
    /\ onModem' = [onModem EXCEPT ![NetOf(m)] = m]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, queued, uploaded>>

\* The token cannot be moved out from under a machine that is keying.
Pass ==
    /\ \A n \in Networks : onModem[n] = IDLE
    /\ token' = (token % MachineCount) + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onModem, queued, uploaded>>

Upload(m) ==
    /\ onModem[NetOf(m)] = m
    /\ uploaded[NetOf(m)] < BatchLimit
    /\ uploaded' = [uploaded EXCEPT ![NetOf(m)] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, onModem, queued>>

Release(m) ==
    /\ onModem[NetOf(m)] = m
    /\ onModem' = [onModem EXCEPT ![NetOf(m)] = IDLE]
    /\ queued' = queued \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, uploaded>>

Next ==
    \/ Pass
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Queue(m) \/ Seize(m) \/ Upload(m) \/ Release(m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

KeyingMachineHoldsTheToken ==
    \A n \in Networks : onModem[n] # IDLE => token = onModem[n]
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    MachineCount = 4
    PerNetwork = 2
    BatchLimit = 2
    IDLE = IDLE

INVARIANT KeyingMachineHoldsTheToken
nl:
A vending operator runs two separate machine networks in one building — the snack network and the cold-drink network — under two independent route controllers that do not coordinate with each other. Both networks report telemetry through a single shared uplink modem installed in the riser. The modem is the critical resource: it has one carrier, and if two machines key it at the same time the traffic is garbage and both batches are lost.

Exclusive use of the modem is arranged with a token ring. Every machine in the building, regardless of which network it belongs to, sits in one ring, and a single transmit token circulates around it. A machine may take the modem only while it is the machine holding the token. Its own controller records that one of its machines is on the modem, so each network knows whether it is currently keying the carrier.

The token only moves while the modem is idle. A machine that has taken the modem holds the token until it lets the modem go, and only then does the token move on to the next machine in the ring — passing the token out from under a machine that is mid-transmission is precisely what would let a machine on the other network key the carrier at the same time.

A machine that has readings to send raises a request; while its network is not on the modem, the machine's own request can be picked up when the token reaches it. Once on the modem the machine uploads telemetry batches, up to the number its buffer holds, and then releases the modem, clearing its request.

The full set of actions is: Queue, in which a machine whose network is not currently on the modem raises a transmit request; Seize, in which the machine holding the token, whose network is idle and which has a request raised, takes the modem and is recorded as its network's current transmitter; Pass, in which the token moves to the next machine in the ring, permitted only while no network is on the modem; Upload, in which the machine on the modem sends one telemetry batch; and Release, in which the machine on the modem lets it go and clears its request.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a network records one of its machines as being on the modem, that machine is the one holding the ring's transmit token, so the two networks can never be keying the shared carrier at the same time.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od8m5p1t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Nodes, MaxTotal, MaxRev, Quorum, MinCap, NOPROP

\* copy: each registrar node's replica, a revision number and the total it
\* carries. open: the single proposal in flight. tally: who has accepted it.
\* cap: the approved credit cap, retuned during the term.
VARIABLES copy, open, tally, cap

vars == <<copy, open, tally, cap>>

Revisions == [rev: 0..MaxRev, total: 0..MaxTotal]

TypeOK ==
    /\ copy \in [Nodes -> Revisions]
    /\ open \in Revisions \cup {NOPROP}
    /\ tally \subseteq Nodes
    /\ cap \in MinCap..MaxTotal

Init ==
    /\ copy = [n \in Nodes |-> [rev |-> 0, total |-> 0]]
    /\ open = NOPROP
    /\ tally = {}
    /\ cap = MinCap

\* The next revision number comes from the highest any node is carrying,
\* not from the last committed one, because partial writes survive abandons.
Highest ==
    LET f[S \in SUBSET Nodes] ==
        IF S = {} THEN 0
        ELSE LET n == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE
                 rest == f[S \ {n}]
             IN IF copy[n].rev > rest THEN copy[n].rev ELSE rest
    IN f[Nodes]

Propose(t) ==
    /\ open = NOPROP
    /\ Highest < MaxRev
    /\ t <= cap
    /\ open' = [rev |-> Highest + 1, total |-> t]
    /\ tally' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<copy, cap>>

Accept(n) ==
    /\ open # NOPROP
    /\ n \notin tally
    /\ copy[n].rev < open.rev
    /\ copy' = [copy EXCEPT ![n] = open]
    /\ tally' = tally \cup {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<open, cap>>

Commit ==
    /\ open # NOPROP
    /\ Cardinality(tally) >= Quorum
    /\ open' = NOPROP
    /\ tally' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<copy, cap>>

\* Abandoning does not undo the writes nodes have already made.
Abandon ==
    /\ open # NOPROP
    /\ Cardinality(tally) < Quorum
    /\ open' = NOPROP
    /\ tally' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<copy, cap>>

Retune ==
    /\ \E c \in MinCap..MaxTotal : cap' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<copy, open, tally>>

AcceptStep == \E n \in Nodes : Accept(n)

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in 0..MaxTotal : Propose(t)
    \/ AcceptStep \/ Commit \/ Abandon \/ Retune

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ WF_vars(AcceptStep) /\ WF_vars(Commit) /\ WF_vars(Abandon)

SameRevisionSameTotal ==
    \A m, n \in Nodes : copy[m].rev = copy[n].rev => copy[m].total = copy[n].total

NoProposalStaysOpen == (open # NOPROP) ~> (open = NOPROP)
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Nodes = {regA, regB, regC}
    MaxTotal = 2
    MaxRev = 2
    Quorum = 2
    MinCap = 1
    NOPROP = NOPROP

INVARIANT SameRevisionSameTotal

PROPERTY NoProposalStaysOpen
nl:
A university keeps each student's degree-audit record — the approved credit total for the term — replicated across several registrar nodes. Advisors edit that total, and because two advisors can be looking at the same student at the same time, an edit that is written blindly can wipe out an edit made a moment earlier. The registrar's rule is that no single node may accept an edit on its own: every edit is put to the nodes and needs a quorum of them before it counts as made.

An edit is proposed as a numbered revision. The proposing advisor reads the highest revision number any node is currently carrying and proposes the next one up; that is what stops a second edit from being written at a revision number that some node has already used for a different value. Only one proposal is open at a time. Nodes then accept it one at a time, and accepting means the node writes the proposed value and revision into its own copy — a node only accepts a revision newer than the one it is already carrying.

A proposal that has reached a quorum of acceptances is committed and closed. A proposal that has not reached quorum can instead be abandoned and closed, which is the awkward case: some nodes may already have written it into their copies, and those partial writes stay. That is exactly why the next proposal takes its number from the highest revision any node carries rather than from the last committed one.

The approved credit cap is retuned during the term as the senate adjusts overload policy, and an advisor may only propose a total that fits the cap in force when the proposal is made.

The full set of actions is: Propose, in which an advisor opens a proposal for the next revision above the highest any node carries, naming a total that fits the current cap, and clears the acceptance tally; Accept, in which a node that is carrying an older revision writes the open proposal into its copy and adds its acceptance; Commit, in which a proposal that has reached quorum is closed as made; Abandon, in which a proposal that has not reached quorum is closed unmade, leaving any partial writes in place; and Retune, in which the senate sets the approved credit cap to any supported value.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any two registrar nodes carrying the same revision number carry the same credit total, so no advisor's edit is ever overwritten by another edit issued at the same revision.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: No proposal stays open forever — every proposal that is opened is eventually closed, either committed once it reaches quorum or abandoned.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od6m8p5t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Cars, Technicians, JournalLimit, NOBODY, CHIEF

\* bankLock: the coarse lock; carLock: the fine per-car lock.
\* sealed: whether a car's single-use charge is still unspent.
\* journal: permanent firing record, with the prior count seen at write time.
VARIABLES bankLock, carLock, sealed, journal

vars == <<bankLock, carLock, sealed, journal>>

Firers == Technicians \cup {CHIEF}
Entries == [car: Cars, by: Firers, priors: 0..JournalLimit]

TypeOK ==
    /\ bankLock \in Technicians \cup {NOBODY}
    /\ carLock \in [Cars -> Technicians \cup {NOBODY}]
    /\ sealed \in [Cars -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ journal \in Seq(Entries)

Init ==
    /\ bankLock = NOBODY
    /\ carLock = [c \in Cars |-> NOBODY]
    /\ sealed = [c \in Cars |-> TRUE]
    /\ journal = <<>>

Priors(c) == Cardinality({i \in 1..Len(journal) : journal[i].car = c})

TakeBank(t) ==
    /\ bankLock = NOBODY
    /\ bankLock' = t
    /\ UNCHANGED <<carLock, sealed, journal>>

\* Picking a car drops the coarse lock in the same step.
TakeCar(t, c) ==
    /\ bankLock = t
    /\ carLock[c] = NOBODY
    /\ carLock' = [carLock EXCEPT ![c] = t]
    /\ bankLock' = NOBODY
    /\ UNCHANGED <<sealed, journal>>

DropBank(t) ==
    /\ bankLock = t
    /\ bankLock' = NOBODY
    /\ UNCHANGED <<carLock, sealed, journal>>

Fire(t, c) ==
    /\ carLock[c] = t
    /\ sealed[c]
    /\ Len(journal) < JournalLimit
    /\ sealed' = [sealed EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
    /\ journal' = Append(journal,
                         [car |-> c, by |-> t, priors |-> Priors(c)])
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bankLock, carLock>>

\* The chief takes no lock at all, but cannot fire a charge that is spent.
Override(c) ==
    /\ sealed[c]
    /\ Len(journal) < JournalLimit
    /\ sealed' = [sealed EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
    /\ journal' = Append(journal,
                         [car |-> c, by |-> CHIEF, priors |-> Priors(c)])
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bankLock, carLock>>

ReleaseCar(t, c) ==
    /\ carLock[c] = t
    /\ carLock' = [carLock EXCEPT ![c] = NOBODY]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bankLock, sealed, journal>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Technicians : TakeBank(t) \/ DropBank(t)
    \/ \E t \in Technicians, c \in Cars :
        TakeCar(t, c) \/ Fire(t, c) \/ ReleaseCar(t, c)
    \/ \E c \in Cars : Override(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

EveryFiringWasTheFirst ==
    \A i \in 1..Len(journal) : journal[i].priors = 0
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Cars = {carLow, carHigh}
    Technicians = {tech1, tech2}
    JournalLimit = 2
    NOBODY = NOBODY
    CHIEF = CHIEF

INVARIANT EveryFiringWasTheFirst
nl:
Each car in a skyscraper's elevator bank carries a single-use pyrotechnic safety brake. Firing it is as irreversible as anything in the building: the charge is spent, the car is clamped to the rails, and it comes off the rails only with a crew and a crane. Firing a car's brake twice is not merely wasteful, it is a certification failure, so every firing is written into the bank's permanent journal along with how many earlier firings that car had already had when the entry was written.

Ordinary maintenance staff reach a car's brake through a two-level lock. A technician must first take the lock on the bank as a whole, and only while holding it may it take the lock on one individual car. Taking the car's lock releases the bank lock immediately, so the coarse lock is held only long enough to pick a car, and other technicians can go on working on other cars. A technician that holds a car's lock may fire that car's brake, provided the car's charge is still sealed, and may release the car's lock when finished. A technician holding the bank lock that decides against picking a car simply drops it.

The building's fire chief has a privileged override. In an alarm the chief fires a car's brake directly, taking no lock at all — not the bank lock and not the car's — because the two-level scheme exists to keep technicians out of each other's way, not to stand between the chief and a car full of people. What the override does not bypass is the charge itself: the chief cannot fire a charge that has already been spent, because there is physically nothing left to fire. The journal has a fixed length and nothing is written once it is full.

The full set of actions is: TakeBank, in which a technician takes the free bank lock; TakeCar, in which a technician holding the bank lock takes a free car lock and drops the bank lock in the same step; DropBank, in which a technician drops the bank lock without picking a car; Fire, in which a technician holding a car's lock fires that car's still-sealed charge, spending it and writing a journal entry recording the car, the technician, and how many earlier firings that car had; Override, in which the fire chief fires a car's still-sealed charge with no lock held, writing the same kind of journal entry; and ReleaseCar, in which a technician gives up a car's lock.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every entry in the bank's journal records that its car had no earlier firings, so no car's safety brake is ever fired a second time.
